This modeling is essential to every phase of the experimental analyses, and the theoretical uncertainties play an important role in interpreting experimental results.In this Review of current challenges, we summarize the open questions in neutrino-nucleus interactions at GeV-scale energies, and discuss in detail the potential impacts of these unknowns on the measurement of neutrino properties, using the determination of oscillation parameters as a central example. After an Executive Summary and a concise Overview of the issues, we address how the neutrino event generators treat these challenges, how electron-nucleus interactions can help understanding these challenges and the important unanswered questions for each underlying physics process---from quasi-elastic to deep-inelastic scattering. Across every topic, we find that current challenges can be met only through active support and collaboration among specialists in strong interactions and electroweak physics, including theorists and experimentalists from both the nuclear and high-energy physics communities.

hep-ph.title: Black-hole ringdown at an exceptional point
hep-ph.author: Kyriakos Destounis
hep-ph.abstract: Black holes ring in damped oscillations. At an exceptional point, photon-sphere and near-horizon modes merge, and their response can acquire a linear time factor. We compute its amplitude from constrained Einstein-Maxwell data for a rotating, charged black hole in de Sitter space. With seven competing modes fixed, the late-time curvature error is 0.00383$\%$ for the pair and 0.01401$\%$ for a refitted exponential. We suppress the linear term by tuning the initial disturbance at fixed geometry. Hence, near coalescence, changing only the initial disturbance can shift the frequency inferred from a short ringdown fit.

hep-ph.title: Self-bound quantum dark fermion stars: saturation, a coupling-capped maximum mass, and tidal signatures of a vector dark sector
hep-ph.author: Ilidio Lopes
hep-ph.abstract: I show that a dark sector whose fermions couple to both a scalar and a vector mediator saturates in close analogy with nuclear matter: the energy per particle develops a minimum at finite density, cold dark matter of this kind is self-bound, and its stars, computed here in full general relativity, possess the sharp surfaces of strange quark stars. Saturation makes the maximum stellar mass a property of the Lagrangian rather than an inheritance of the Chandrasekhar scaling: it rises eightfold across the saturation window, which a critical vector coupling closes, so the theory caps its own maximum mass, at $3.9\,M_\odot$ for a fermion of $1\,\mathrm{GeV}$ and the fiducial saturation density, a ceiling shared by the whole family of couplings rather than by any single parameter set. Metastable couplings support two disconnected stable families, one dilute and gravitationally bound, the other dense and self-bound. The quantum-pressure correction, confined by saturation to a surface layer a few Compton wavelengths thick, governs the smallest dark nuggets whilst shifting stellar masses by less than one part in $10^{21}$. A $1.4\,M_\odot$ member of the fiducial family has a radius of $13.3\,\mathrm{km}$, a compactness of $0.155$, and a tidal deformability of $1.6\times 10^{3}$, almost an order of magnitude above the measured neutron-star value, so at a given particle mass and couplings a single well-measured inspiral distinguishes these stars from neutron stars and from their scalar-only counterparts, whilst the deformability surviving at the maximum mass separates them, in principle, from black holes.

hep-ph.title: Stochastic Acceleration Downstream of Astrophysical Shocks
hep-ph.author: Antonio Capanema, Pasquale Blasi
hep-ph.abstract: Generation and evolution of turbulence at shock fronts are crucial aspects of the process of particle acceleration in different classes of sources. Here we aim at describing the fate of non-thermal particles and turbulence in the downstream region of an astrophysical shock, both in the case in which turbulence is solely produced upstream and advected through the shock and in the case in which additional turbulence is injected downstream. In particular we will provide an estimate of the effect of stochastic acceleration on particles accelerated at the shock and then advected behind it. The calculations will be specialized to supernova remnant shocks. The temporal evolution of the particle distribution function downstream of the shock and the power spectrum of the turbulent perturbations are both followed by solving numerically the transport equations for the two quantities, accounting for the damping of waves due to the particles that resonantly interact with them, which makes the problem non-linear. Our calculations show that, if waves are only self-generated upstream via Bell instability, they are not able to significantly modify the particle spectrum in the downstream region. Additionally, turbulent cascading in $k$-space quickly drains their energy, further limiting the stochastic acceleration of particles. If, on the other hand, there are additional sources of turbulence downstream, then these waves can contribute meaningfully to second order Fermi acceleration and alter the spectrum of particles. This may reflect in the spectrum of gamma radiation produced through $pp$ scattering downstream. Although second order Fermi acceleration is typically slower than diffusive shock acceleration, particles are expected to stay downstream of shocks for much longer times during which stochastic acceleration can modify their spectrum and affect the spectra of multi-messenger emissions.

hep-ph.title: Constrained field-space estimators for background-field lattice QCD observables
hep-ph.author: Scott Moerschbacher, Frank X. Lee
hep-ph.abstract: Background-field lattice calculations extract weak-field response coefficients from correlators computed at several field strengths. We treat this extraction as linear estimation in field space and compare fixed cancellation stencils with covariance-optimized, generalized-least-squares estimators of the same coefficient, using archival nucleon double ratios on about 1000 quenched configurations at six quark masses and decuplet correlators for which exact answers follow from the lattice contractions. The fixed $O(B^4)$-$O(B^8)$ stencils are nearly coincident and cost almost nothing in precision. Weight-free null-space tests reject the two-term response model in most nucleon ensembles; whether they reject the three-term model depends on the temporal fits and on the noise of the estimated temporal covariance, which raises the null-contrast error by a factor of 1.7-2.4. With that noise included, covariance optimization gains 1-2% in precision at the five lighter masses (3-30% with two-state time fits, which also lower moments by 3-10%) and nothing on independent data halves, while its weights carry three to four orders of magnitude more leverage on omitted response modes than the fixed stencils and move the moments by up to 1.8 marginal standard errors. The decuplet controls show what such leverage does under misspecification: the first-order responses obey $\mu_{\Delta^+}/\mu_{\Delta^{++}}=1/2$ and $\mu_{\Delta^0}=0$ exactly. The lowest-order estimate misses the first by 10-25 standard errors. The fixed $O(B^4)$-$O(B^8)$ stencils satisfy it within errors in the production windows, whereas the correlated linear fit in $B^2$, with the same constraints as the $O(B^4)$ stencil, misses it by 3-17%; the null-space test rejects that fit's model. The results distinguish statistical precision from robustness to omitted response modes; they are not physical-point magnetic moments.

hep-ph.title: Flavor decomposition of the nucleon axial and tensor charges from lattice QCD
hep-ph.author: C. Alexandrou(Univ. of Cyprus & The Cyprus Inst.), S. Bacchio(The Cyprus Inst.), M. Di Carlo(Roma Tor Vergata), A. Evangelista(Univ. of Cyprus), C. Iona(Univ. of Cyprus & The Cyprus Inst.), F. Pittler(The Cyprus Inst.), G. Spanoudes(Univ. of Cyprus)
hep-ph.abstract: We determine the nucleon axial and tensor charges using four ensembles of twisted-mass clover-improved fermions with approximately equal physical volumes of about 5.5~fm and four lattice spacings, $ a=0.05$~fm, 0.06~fm, 0.07~fm, and 0.08~fm. The mass of the degenerate up and down, strange and charm quarks are tuned to approximately their physical values. We compute both connected and disconnected contributions to determine the isovector and isoscalar charges and their flavour decomposition. For the nucleon isovector axial charge we find $g_A^{u-d}=1.263(34)(26)$, in agreement with the experimental value. For the isoscalar axial charge we find $g_A^{u+d}=0.458(16)(1)$, while for the corresponding tensor charges we find $g_T^{u-d}=0.951(21)(5)$ and $g_T^{u+d}=0.556(16)(5)$.

hep-ph.title: Elliptic flow of $ϕ$ and $Ω$ via quark recombination mechanism in relativistic heavy-ion collisions
hep-ph.author: Zhidong Yang, Lie-Wen Chen
hep-ph.abstract: Multi-strange hadrons, such as the $\phi$ meson and $\Omega$ baryon, serve as unique probes for the properties of the quark-gluon plasma in relativistic heavy-ion collisions. Using a quark recombination model with the quark phase-space information parameterized in a viscous blastwave, we show that the elliptic flow $v_2$ of $\phi$ and $\Omega$ can be describled by quark recombination in a wide energy range from $\sqrt{s_{NN}}$ = 7.7 GeV to 5.02 TeV. We check the scaling properties of $v_2$ of $\phi$ and $\Omega$ and find the number-of-constituent-quark (NCQ) scaled $v_2$ of $\phi$ and $\Omega$ are approximately equal. We further present the $v_2$ of strange quarks at hadronization extracted from $\phi$ and $\Omega$ data. We find the $v_2$ of strange quarks is close to the NCQ-scaled $v_2$ of $\phi$ and $\Omega$ at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}$ = 7.7-200 GeV, but significant larger than the latter at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}$ = 2.76-5.02 TeV, suggesting that the $v_2$ of strange quarks cannot be simply equated to the NCQ-scaled $v_2$ of $\phi$ and $\Omega$. Our results demonstrate that the quark recombination mechanism is valid for $\phi$ and $\Omega$ production in heavy-ion collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}$ = 7.7 GeV to 5.02 TeV, indicating the existence of constituent quark degree of freedom at these energies.

hep-ph.title: The Fate of Collisional Neutrino Flavor Conversion: Fixed Points, Period Doubling, and Chaos
hep-ph.author: Jiabao Liu, Lucas Johns, Hiroki Nagakura
hep-ph.abstract: Core-collapse supernovae and neutron star mergers are among the most energetic astrophysical events and promising sources of multimessenger signals. Their dynamics and nucleosynthesis depend sensitively on neutrino transport, yet the impact of neutrino flavor evolution in these dense environments remains poorly understood. Predicting the outcome of collisional flavor instability (CFI) remains a challenge, despite progress in local-relaxation methods for fast flavor conversion. Here we construct homogeneous collective-precession states with stationary flavor populations in two-flavor quantum kinetics with collisional relaxation. The method applies to arbitrary energy spectra and energy-dependent collision rates. Our numerical examples exhibit persistent oscillations and a period-doubling route to chaos. Even in these regimes, the stationary populations estimate the time-averaged flavor populations to within $10\%$ in our tests. These fixed points provide a physically motivated input for incorporating CFI into astrophysical simulations, with implications for neutrino heating and ejecta nucleosynthesis.

hep-ph.title: Machine learning assisted $ν/\barν$ discrimination in atmospheric neutrino events for CPV sensitivity in a 20-kton liquid scintillator detector
hep-ph.author: Dek Hao Liew, Mohammad Nizam, Shu Tian Eu, Siew Yan Hoh
hep-ph.abstract: Atmospheric neutrinos span a broad range of energies and baselines, offering a complementary probe of leptonic CP violation. However, a JUNO-like liquid scintillator detector without a magnetic field cannot directly separate neutrino and antineutrino interactions, reducing CP violation sensitivity. This study investigates whether machine learning based statistical separation can improve CP violation sensitivity in a 20-kton detector. $\nu_{\mu}$ and $\nu_e$ charged current events are generated with GENIE (using Honda flux) in a JUNO-like detector geometry and are reweighted using OscProb three flavor oscillation probabilities incorporating Earth matter effects and NuFIT parameters. Detector response is approximated by smearing lepton and hadronic energies, neutrino direction, and neutron multiplicity. Logistic regression, XGBoost, and multilayer perceptron (MLP) classifiers are trained on inelasticity, neutron multiplicity, and charged lepton energy, with XGBoost selected for the analysis. CP violation sensitivity is evaluated for a 200 kton-year exposure using a Poisson likelihood with systematic nuisance parameters and marginalization over five oscillation parameters within their respective $3\sigma$ ranges. XGBoost achieves an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of approximately 0.83 for both flavor samples. Under the square root approximation, peak CP violation sensitivity improves from 1.49 $\sigma$ to 1.96 $\sigma$ for normal mass ordering and from 1.14 $\sigma$ to 1.61 $\sigma$ for inverted mass ordering. Machine learning based statistical neutrino-antineutrino separation can recover part of the CP violation sensitivity lost in charge blind detectors. These preliminary results motivate further studies incorporating validated detector response and systematic uncertainties.

hep-ph.title: Quasinormal Modes of Black holes in the generalized Schwarzschild-de Sitter solution of $f(R)$ gravity
hep-ph.author: Dhruba Jyoti Gogoi, Himanshu Chaudhary, Tiberiu Harko
hep-ph.abstract: We analyze scalar, vector, and {axial} tensor perturbations in a Schwarzschild-type static spherically symmetric solution of modified $f(R)$ gravity. This solution differs from the Schwarzschild metric of general relativity through the presence of a linearly growing term and a logarithmic correction, and it depends on four integration constants. Using the higher-order Wentzel-Kramers-Brillouin (WKB) approximation and an analytical method, we calculate the quasinormal modes (QNMs) for all three types of perturbations. Our results show that, for appropriately chosen parameter values, the QNMs closely match those of the Schwarzschild black hole. In particular, the model parameter $A$ produces a nonlinear increase in both the oscillation frequency and damping rate of ringdown gravitational waves. A similar effect arises for the parameter $\eta$ when $A$ is small, while for larger $A$ values the effects are opposite, where the scalar perturbations display a distinct deviation compared to the vector and {axial} tensor cases. Contour plots of QNMs in the parameter space support these findings. Finally, time-domain profiles are obtained to illustrate the dynamical evolution of the gravitational wave signal.

hep-ph.title: Measurements of $C\!P$ violation with charm hadrons at Belle and Belle II
hep-ph.author: Jaeyoung Kim(on behalf of the Belle II Collaboration)
hep-ph.abstract: Recent searches for $C\!P$ violation in charm-hadron decays at Belle and Belle II are presented. The measurements cover $D^+_{(s)}\to\eta h^+$, $D\to\pi\pi$, $D^0\to K_S^0K_S^0$, and $D^0\to\pi^+\pi^-\pi^0$, together with the singly Cabibbo-suppressed baryon decays $\Xi_c^+\to\Sigma^+h^+h^-$ and $\Lambda_c^+\to ph^+h^-$, where $h=\pi,K$. The Belle II analyses use the Run~1 data sample of $428\,\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$, supplemented by $980\,\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$ of Belle data for the $K_S^0K_S^0$ measurements. We report preliminary results for the $\eta h^+$ modes, complementary tests of the isospin structure of $D\to\pi\pi$, and an application of inclusive charm-flavor tagging. The first individual decay-rate asymmetries in these three-body charmed-baryon modes also provide tests of $U$-spin symmetry. All reported asymmetries are consistent with $C\!P$ symmetry within the present precision.

hep-ph.title: Renormalized symmetry probes for emergent symmetries and non-chiral lattice fermions
hep-ph.author: Ting-Wai Chiu
hep-ph.abstract: The degeneracy of hadron correlators in symmetry-related channels signals symmetry restoration in high-temperature QCD. RG-invariant probes of this degeneracy need care when the regularization breaks chiral symmetry, or when the symmetry is not exact in the massless action, as for the emergent chiral-spin symmetry $SU(2)_{CS}$. We renormalize the thermal and screening meson correlators of every flavor sector by the thermal correlator of the same channel in the $\bar ud$ sector at a common reference point. The symmetry ratio $\kappa_{AB}$ then depends on the renormalization only through the ratio $R_{AB}$. For exact symmetries, $R_{AB}=1$ and $\kappa_{AB}$ is RG invariant and scheme independent in mass-independent schemes. For emergent symmetries, $R_{AB}\neq1$ carries the relative logarithmic cutoff dependence of the two channels, which cancels in $\kappa_{AB}$, and the residual dependence on the reference scale is physical. The framework applies to Wilson, twisted-mass and staggered fermions, where $R_{AB}$ absorbs the channel-dependent renormalization, and the tensor pair $(T_k,X_k)$ keeps $R_{T_kX_k}=1$ on isotropic Wilson-type lattices. Lattice artifacts are a small correction to the chiral-spin probes $\kappa_{CS}$ and $\kappa_{fade}$, but as large as the signal of the exact-symmetry probes. For free quarks, we derive $\kappa_{fade}=2/3$ for every mass and separation, and $\kappa_{CS}\le1/3$. We apply the renormalized probes to $N_f=2+1+1$ QCD with optimal domain-wall quarks at the physical point, with $a=0.064$ fm and $T=192$-$1539$ MeV. The hierarchical restoration of the chiral symmetries from the light to the charm sectors is confirmed, and is invariant under renormalization. The $\bar uc$ and $\bar sc$ sectors have the widest chiral-spin windows, also at a tighter threshold. Thus spin-1 mesons with one charm quark are the most attractive channels for the chiral-spin regime.

hep-ph.title: Deep Inelastic Scattering and Proton Structure Functions in AdS/QCD models
hep-ph.author: Rafael A. Costa-Silva, Henrique Boschi-Filho
hep-ph.abstract: In this work we study the holographical fermionic deep inelastic scattering in a deformed AdS model. Imposing that the potentials that emerge from the Schrödinger-like equations for the fermionic chiral left and right modes are SUSY partners to preserve isospectrality, we implement a systematical truncation of such potentials. Then, we show that in the quadratic approximation of the deformed AdS model, the fermionic DIS and the proton structure functions $F_{1,2}(q^2,x)$ are identical with the results obtained from the soft wall model. Further, we obtain and compare high-order approximations for the fermionic potentials with the full solution of the deformed AdS model and show, as expected, that as greater the order of approximation, the better are the results for $F_{1,2}(q^2,x)$ when compared with experimental data explicitly for the Bjorken parameter values $x=0.85, 0.75$ and $0.65$.

hep-ph.title: Unpolarized proton PDF with physical quark masses and large momenta
hep-ph.author: Xiang Gao, Andrew Hanlon, Jinchen He, Xiangyu Jiang, Swagato Mukherjee, Peter Petreczky, Qi Shi, Yong Zhao
hep-ph.abstract: We present a lattice quantum chromodynamics (QCD) calculation of the proton isovector ($u-d$) unpolarized parton distribution function (PDF) at physical sea and valence quark masses, using Coulomb-gauge-fixed quark bilinears within the large-momentum effective theory framework. The calculation is performed on a (2+1)-flavor ensemble with a lattice spacing of $a=0.076$ fm and proton momenta up to $2.3$ GeV. We combine kinematically enhanced nucleon interpolating operators, the Coulomb-gauge method, and high-statistics measurements to improve the signal quality at large momenta and quark separations. We use the static regularization-independent momentum subtraction and hybrid schemes to renormalize the bare matrix elements. The light-cone PDF in the $\overline{\rm MS}$ scheme is obtained from the quasi-PDF through next-to-leading-order (NLO) perturbative matching supplemented by next-to-leading-logarithmic renormalization-group resummation. With reduced uncertainties, the resulting PDF is consistent with our previous calculation on a similar lattice ensemble with $a=0.06$~fm and a valence pion mass of 300 MeV. Notably, despite the reduced uncertainties, the agreement with the phenomenological PDF persists over the longitudinal momentum fraction range $0.25\lesssim|x|\lesssim0.75$, where the lattice calculation is expected to be reliable. This agreement is further supported by a comparison in coordinate space, where our short-distance lattice matrix elements are consistent with those obtained from the phenomenological PDF through NLO matching. In particular, we observe close agreement in the imaginary part for the first time. Together, these results represent an encouraging step toward precision benchmarking of lattice QCD calculations of PDFs.

hep-ph.title: Isospin violation and the neutron weak magnetic moment
hep-ph.author: Gerald A. Miller
hep-ph.abstract: The recent measurement of weak magnetism in neutron beta decay [1] obtained a value that is consistent with the conserved vector current hypothesis requiring the assumption of isospin conservation. The influence of the quark-mass difference and electromagnetic effects that violate this conservation law are examined using non-relativistic constituent quark models and estimated to be of the order of at most 1%.

hep-ph.title: Little Red Dots from Primordial Black Holes: Non-Gaussianity and Accretion Evade $μ$-Distortion Constraints
hep-ph.author: Shyam Balaji, Bryce Cyr, Sarah R. Geller, David I. Kaiser, Dario L. Lorenzoni, Evan McDonough, Wenzer Qin
hep-ph.abstract: Recent JWST observations of "Little Red Dots" (LRDs) at $z \gtrsim 4$ suggest the existence of early supermassive black holes (SMBHs) with masses $\gtrsim 10^6\,M_\odot$. Their rapid emergence challenges conventional seeding and growth scenarios based on accretion and mergers of Population III stellar remnants, motivating renewed interest in primordial black holes (PBHs) formed from primordial perturbations. Explaining such massive seeds requires power spectrum enhancements that are constrained by cosmic microwave background (CMB) spectral distortions. In this work we perform the first comprehensive Bayesian exploration of non-Gaussian primordial perturbations capable of producing SMBH seeds while remaining consistent with CMB spectral distortion constraints, and examine the role of accretion history in constraining these models. We perform a suite of Markov chain Monte Carlo analyses of power spectrum enhancements (lognormal and cut-power-law) with varying local non-Gaussianity and accretion histories, satisfying the COBE/FIRAS $\mu$-distortion constraint with and without the requirement that the model produces SMBH seeds. We find that both models can seed LRDs and evade $\mu$-distortion bounds for $|f_{\rm NL}|= O(1)$ and peak amplitude $A= O(10^{-3})$, when standard Eddington-limited accretion is also incorporated. Interestingly, the results exhibit a preference for both positive and negative values of $f_{\rm NL}$. The preference for negative $f_{\rm NL}$ is strongly dependent on the accretion history, and is removed if the black holes have a small duty cycle, $f_{\rm duty}\lesssim 0.1$. These results demonstrate that the JWST high-$z$ LRD population can be seeded by primordial perturbations while remaining compatible with CMB data, and highlight the importance of next-generation CMB spectral distortion missions to test this hypothesis.

hep-ph.title: One-loop soft anomalous dimension matrices for $t\bar t j$ hadroproduction
hep-ph.author: Bakar Chargeishvili, Maria Vittoria Garzelli, Sven-Olaf Moch
hep-ph.abstract: We calculate the one-loop corrections to the soft anomalous dimension matrices for the production of a top-antitop quark pair in association with a jet at hadron colliders. This is a step forward towards implementing a procedure for the resummation of soft-gluon emission logarithms for the $t\bar{t}j + X$ hadroproduction process, that will enable the improvement of the accuracy of the $t\bar{t} j + X$ cross sections, beyond the current degree of knowledge. The latter, so far, has reached the next-to-leading order (NLO) level, complemented by the accuracy of the Shower Monte Carlo approaches used in matching the NLO computations to parton showers (PS) and by merging with matrix elements with a different number of light jets.

hep-ph.title: Phenomenological revisit of the $B$ ${\to}$ $ππ$ decays by incorporating soft color-octet contributions
hep-ph.author: Yueling Yang, Bingbing Yang, Junfeng Sun
hep-ph.abstract: Motivated by the long-standing ``${\pi}{\pi}$ puzzle'' in nonleptonic $B$ decays, we revisit the $B$ ${\to}$ ${\pi}{\pi}$ decays within the QCD factorization (QCDF) framework, now incorporating the soft color-octet matrix element (COME) contributions, an ingredient that has been largely overlooked in earlier QCDF studies. A comprehensive phenomenological analysis is performed under three distinct scenarios, with the free parameters determined via fits to the available experimental data using the ${\chi}^{2}$ method. The goodness-of-fit is very poor for Scenario S1, which corresponds to the traditional QCDF case without the soft COME contributions, and for Scenario S2, which includes the soft COME contributions but omits the weak annihilation (WA) contributions. Scenario S3, in which both the COME and WA contributions are included simultaneously, achieves an excellent overall fit. In Scenario S3, the QCDF approach can accommodate almost all $B$ ${\to}$ ${\pi}{\pi}$ observables in a consistent and satisfactory manner, and the fitted parameters ${\rho}_{A}$ $<$ $1$ (WA) and ${\rho}_{c}$ ${\sim}$ $0.3$ (soft COME) are in good agreement with the QCDF power counting scheme and the factorization hypothesis.

hep-ph.title: Atmospheric Mass-Squared Splitting at Sub-Percent Precision as a $CPT$ Symmetry Probe
hep-ph.author: T. V. Ngoc, S. Cao, P. T. Quyen
hep-ph.abstract: In this paper, we present an one of the most sensitive test of $CPT$ symmetry in the leptonic sector by probing the atmospheric neutrino mass-squared splittings, $\Delta m^2_{31}$ and $\Delta \overline{m}^2_{31}$, using simulated data from on-going reactor-based JUNO and future accelerator-based DUNE and Hyper-Kamiokande experiments. Our study focuses on the potential neutrino-antineutrino mass asymmetry $\delta_{\nu\overline{\nu}}(\Delta m^2_{31}) = \Delta m^2_{31} - \Delta \overline{m}^2_{31}$, achieving unprecedented precision by exploiting the high statistics and reduced systematic uncertainties of these facilities. The combined analysis yields a projected sensitivity to $CPT$ violation at the level of $\sim 1.7\times 10^{-5}~\text{eV}^2$ at $3\sigma$ confidence level. These results highlight the crucial role of multi-experiment synergies in testing fundamental symmetries of nature. The work also investigates impact of potential bias on the (anti-)neutrino mass-splitting measurement due to the neutrino interactions with accelerator-based neutrino experiments, and conclude that it must be improved by at least $39\%$ compared to T2K simulated-benchmark to achieve a sub-percent precision probe of $CPT$ violation.

hep-ph.title: Information-Theoretic Gaps in Solar and Reactor Neutrino Oscillation Measurements
hep-ph.author: Neetu Raj Singh Chundawat, Yu-Feng Li
hep-ph.abstract: Quantum estimation theory provides a fundamental framework for analyzing how precisely physical parameters can be estimated from measurements. Neutrino oscillations are characterized by a set of parameters inferred from experiments conducted in different production and detection environments. The two solar oscillation parameters, $\Delta m^2_{21}$ and $\theta_{12}$, can be estimated using both solar neutrino experiments and reactor neutrino experiments. In this letter, we use Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) to quantify and compare the information content accessible in these two experimental setups. For reactor neutrinos, flavor measurements saturate the QFI for both parameters over relevant energy ranges, demonstrating that ideal measurements could achieve ultimate quantum precision bound. In contrast, for solar neutrinos the phase-based QFI vanishes, originating from the quantum coherence, rendering the estimation of $\Delta m_{21}^2$ purely population-based and effectively classical, while the QFI for $\theta_{12}$ remains sizable and nearly saturated by flavor measurements at high energies. Consequently, solar experiments are intrinsically more sensitive to $\theta_{12}$ than to $\Delta m_{21}^2$, reflecting a fundamental difference in the information encoded in the two systems.

hep-ph.title: Hidden-charm $uds\,c\bar c$ pentaquarks as flavor eigenstates in a constituent quark model
hep-ph.author: M.C. Gordillo, J.M. Alcaraz-Pelegrina, J. Segovia
hep-ph.abstract: We use a diffusion Monte Carlo (DMC) algorithm to solve the Schrödinger equation describing $udsc\bar c$ pentaquarks within a non-relativistic constituent quark model. We consider multiquark states with well-defined parity, color, spin and isospin quantum numbers, consistent with the experimentally favored assignment $J^P = 1/2^-$ for one of the observed candidates, and impose $I = 0$. We find that, in order to reproduce the presence of multiple structures in the experimental mass region, the total wavefunction must also be an eigenstate of the SU(3) flavor operator. Under this condition, two structures emerge with masses lying in the same region as the experimentally observed signals in the $J/\psi\,\Lambda$ spectrum. In addition, two states are predicted below the $J/\psi\,\Lambda$ threshold but above the $\eta_c\,\Lambda$ one, which would not contribute to that channel. If only the $I = 0$ condition is imposed, a single structure is obtained, with a mass below the $J/\psi\,\Lambda$ threshold.

hep-ph.title: Lepton Mixing from a Lattice Flavon Model: A Two-Branch Octant-delta Prediction
hep-ph.author: Vernon Barger
hep-ph.abstract:
We extend the single-flavon $B$-lattice Froggatt-Nielsen (FN) framework, previously applied to quark masses and CKM mixing, to the lepton sector. The same $B$-lattice power structure ($\epsilon\equiv 1/B\simeq 0.19$) generates charged-lepton mass hierarchies and a normal-ordered neutrino spectrum; large neutrino mixing angles require an additional mu-tau reflection symmetry of the neutrino mass matrix, which fixes the atmospheric angle to $45^\circ$ and the neutrino-sector Dirac phase to $\delta_
u=270^\circ$ exactly while leaving the reactor angle, generated at $\mathcal{O}(\epsilon)$, free. The Pontecorvo-Maki-Nakagawa-Sakata (PMNS) matrix factorizes as $U_{m PMNS}=U_e^\dagger U_
u$, with near-tribimaximal $U_
u$ corrected by small charged-lepton rotations whose $12$ and $23$ phases are aligned. A single interference relation expresses the observed Dirac phase $\delta$ as the maximal neutrino phase shifted by a calculable charged-lepton correction, and correlates the sign of that shift with the atmospheric octant; this produces a two-branch prediction in the $(	heta_{23},\delta)$ plane: a lower-octant branch with $	heta_{23}\approx 44^\circ$, $\delta\approx 260^\circ$, and an upper-octant branch with $	heta_{23}\approx 46^\circ$, $\delta\approx 275^\circ$. The lower octant contains the strict single-source point of the flavon phase. Both branches place $\delta$ within about $15^\circ$ of $270^\circ$, i.e., near-maximal leptonic CP violation, favored by T2K; a Dirac phase in the first or second quadrant, or more than about $40^\circ$ from maximal, would exclude the framework. The Jarlskog invariant $J_{m CP}\simeq -0.033$ is nearly branch-independent; only precision measurements of the atmospheric octant and Dirac phase at DUNE, Hyper-Kamiokande, IceCube, and JUNO can distinguish the two branches.

hep-ph.title: Determining the NJL Coupling and AMM in Magnetized QCD Matter via Machine Learning
hep-ph.author: Zigeng Ding, Fan Lin, Xinyang Wang
hep-ph.abstract: In this study, we investigate the phase structure of magnetized QCD matter by determining the field-dependent parameters of the Nambu-Jona-Lasinio (NJL) model through a physics-informed machine learning framework. Specifically, we focus on extracting the optimal functional forms for the running coupling constant $G(eB)$ and the quark anomalous magnetic moment (AMM) ratio $v_2(eB)$, using lattice QCD computation on the chiral transition and condensate behavior. By embedding the NJL gap equation as a differentiable physics-constrained module, our neural network pipeline identifies continuous parameter functions that accurately reproduce the inverse magnetic catalysis (IMC) effect. Our results demonstrate that the magnetic field smoothly suppresses both $G$ and $v_2$. This approach not only bridges the gap between effective models and lattice data but also provides new microscopic insights into the response of the QCD vacuum to strong magnetic fields. As an independent test, the neutral-pion mass is calculated with the mean learned parameters and reproduces the decreasing trend of recent lattice results without a pion-data refit.

hep-ph.title: Applying self-organizing maps to nonresonant searches
hep-ph.author: Vaidehi Tikhe, N. Kirutheeka, Sourabh Dube
hep-ph.abstract: An excess of events seen in a nonresonant search at a collider can be difficult to ascribe to a specific hypothesis from amongst several competing ones. We explore a novel approach of applying self-organizing maps to such an excess to uniquely identify a hypothesis. We use a search for vector-like leptons in a trilepton final state to outline the method. We define an approach combining the inherent clustering of these maps and elements of supervised learning. We compare the performance of this approach with a multiclassifying neural network. We find that the method using self-organizing maps competes well (despite not using any standard model processes in the training), and provides additional tools that would help characterize any observed excesses in searches.

hep-ph.title: Axion Quality in Warped Extra-Dimension
hep-ph.author: Kiwoon Choi, Chang Hyeon Lee, Chang Sub Shin
hep-ph.abstract: We investigate the axion quality problem in warped extra-dimensional models in which the QCD axion arises as the Wilson-line mode of a five-dimensional $U(1)$ gauge field compactified on an $S^1/\mathbb{Z}_2$ orbifold. Higher-dimensional gauge invariance severely constrains possible sources of Peccei--Quinn symmetry breaking, implying that non-QCD contributions to the axion potential are predominantly generated by nonlocal effects mediated by $U(1)$-charged fields propagating along the compact dimension. We systematically compute these contributions and examine how both the warped geometry and the orbifold fixed points (branes) affect the resulting axion quality. Finally, we classify the parametric suppression of the induced axion potential, thereby identifying the conditions under which warped extra-dimensional axions can achieve sufficiently high quality.

hep-ph.title: Exact baryon-meson relation for $b \to s ν\barν$
hep-ph.author: Teppei Kitahara, Manas Kumar Mohapatra, Kota Sasaki

hep-ph.title: Final-state rescattering in $\bar{B}^{0}_{(s)}\to Λ^{+}_{c}\barΛ^{-}_{c}$ decays
hep-ph.author: Zhu-Ding Duan, Xiao Huang, Dong-Hao Li, Run-Hui Li, Jian-Peng Wang, Fu-Sheng Yu
hep-ph.abstract: The LHCb Collaboration has recently reported the first observation of the decay \(\bar B_s^0\to \Lambda_c^+\bar\Lambda_c^-\), along with measurements of the branching fractions for both \(\bar B^0\to \Lambda_c^+\bar\Lambda_c^-\) and \(\bar B_s^0\to \Lambda_c^+\bar\Lambda_c^-\). In this work, we investigate these two decays within the framework of final state re-scattering. Our results show that the predicted branching fractions are consistent with the experimental measurements, which indicates the significant role of long-distance final-state interactions in such baryonic $B$ decays. Furthermore, we present predictions for the direct CP asymmetries and the asymmetry parameters. Numerically, both decays exhibit nearly vanishing direct CP asymmetries and suppressed longitudinal polarizations $\alpha$, whereas the sizable values of $\beta$ and $\gamma$ reflect strong interference between the two helicity amplitudes and provide sensitive probes of the decay dynamics.

hep-ph.title: Semileptonic sum rules in heavy-to-light charm decays
hep-ph.author: Motoi Endo, Syuhei Iguro, Satoshi Mishima, Takeru Uchiyama, Ryoutaro Watanabe

hep-ph.title: Joint probes of dark matter annihilation from neutrino detectors and CMB targets
hep-ph.author: Ruifeng Leng, Shao-Ping Li
hep-ph.abstract: Dark matter (DM) annihilation into neutrinos provides a promising observational channel targeted by current and forthcoming neutrino detectors. However, the detection of such neutrino fluxes alone cannot uniquely determine their astrophysical or cosmological origin, such as the recent observations from Super-Kamiokande that hint at a small excess of electron antineutrino events. We propose that the effective number of neutrino species and the spectral distortion of the cosmic microwave background (CMB) can serve as complementary observables to probe neutrino signatures from DM annihilation. Using a simple model-independent analysis, we determine the detection windows of these cosmic observables that overlap with the experimental sensitivities from the Super-Kamiokande, Jiangmen Underground Neutrino Observatory, Hyper-Kamiokande, and the Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment, showing that joint probes of large DM annihilation to neutrinos with MeV-GeV masses can be achieved by neutrino detectors and CMB experiments.

hep-ph.title: Revisiting the Axial Anomaly and Chiral Magnetic Effect in Dense Matter, with Applications to Axion Dark Matter
hep-ph.author: Deog Ki Hong
hep-ph.abstract: We explicitly compute the axial anomaly in dense matter and show that it takes the same form as in vacuum, even in the massless limit. This result follows from a subtle cancellation in the anomalous Ward identity between the medium-induced contributions to the divergence of the axial current and to the pseudoscalar density. We then revisit the chiral magnetic effect in a fermionic medium coupled to an axial chemical potential in an external magnetic field. We show that, in the clean limit, the medium supports a persistent, conserved anomalous current carried by fermions. The current is determined by the axial chemical potential and suppressed by the Fermi velocity, in agreement with anomalous axial-current correlation functions. Finally, we discuss applications to axion physics, where axion dark matter acts as an effective axial chemical potential, and estimate how helicity relaxation by impurity scattering limits the induced current in realistic conductors.

hep-ph.title: Taming Symbolic IBP Reduction with Intermediate Bases
hep-ph.author: Qian Song
hep-ph.abstract: Despite many years of development in integration-by-parts reduction, reconstructing all reduction coefficients, which are rational polynomials of kinematic variables and the space-time dimension, remains a non-trivial problem. The main difficulty comes from the large number of unknowns in a general ansatz, which can lead to a linear system that is too large to solve. In this paper, we present an algorithm for reconstructing reduction coefficients through a sequence of intermediate bases. The resulting analytic reduction coefficients are products of a few analytic matrices, whose non-zero entries are simple rational polynomials. We demonstrate the efficiency of this algorithm with two cutting edge examples: a three-point massive box-triangle and a four-point massive pentagon-triangle. Reconstructing all reduction coefficients for the box-triangle (pentagon-triangle) requires 3289 (13013) numerical samplings, significantly fewer than the number of unknowns in the general ansatz, 1407406 (21638331).

hep-ph.title: Fermion mass relations in one-parameter modular models
hep-ph.author: Salvador Centelles Chuliá, Xueqi Li, Xiang-Gan Liu, Omar Medina, J. T. Penedo
hep-ph.abstract: Modular flavour symmetries provide a possible organizing principle for the Standard Model Yukawa sector, by replacing generic couplings with a potentially small number of modular forms controlled by a single complex modulus. We study the extreme limit of this idea: One-Parameter Models, in which each charged-fermion mass matrix is fixed by a single modular invariant contraction. We develop a systematic method to construct such models, showing that the One-Parameter Model requirement is already highly constraining at the level of possible fermion hierarchies. In a concrete realization, the charged-lepton and down-quark sectors are controlled by the common modulus, leading to exact mass relations at the flavour scale, $m_s^5 = 2\sqrt{2}\,m_d^3m_b^2, \qquad m_\mu^3 = \sqrt{2}\,m_e m_\tau^2, \qquad m_s^2m_\tau = \sqrt{2}\,m_e m_b^2$. We show that, once renormalization-group evolution and selective supersymmetric threshold effects are included, these high-scale relations can be made compatible with low-energy charged-fermion data. Our results provide a working proof of principle for One-Parameter Models and point towards a possible route to the flavour puzzle through highly constrained constructions.

hep-ph.title: Holographic light-quark energy loss in a spinning plasma
hep-ph.author: Yan-Qing Zhao, Zhou-Run Zhu
hep-ph.abstract: In this work, we investigate light-quark energy loss in a strongly coupled plasma described by a spinning black-brane background obtained from the large-black-hole limit of the Myers-Perry geometry. The parameter $a$ characterizes the boost/rotation parameter of the dual fluid in this holographic setup and is related to the angular velocity in the corresponding limit. We employ two complementary probes, the falling-string and shooting-string descriptions, to compute the stopping distance and the instantaneous energy loss of a light quark moving either transverse or parallel to the local tangential-flow direction. The results show that light quarks quench more readily in a hot environment. For parallel propagation, a counter-propagating configuration enhances energy loss, whereas a co-propagating configuration suppresses it. For transverse propagation, increasing the magnitude of the rotational motion promotes energy loss. In addition, the instantaneous energy loss increases along the trajectory of the endpoint. These results describe classical probe dynamics in the local planar limit and do not include intrinsic-spin effects.

hep-ph.title: Exclusive Quark and Gluon Dijet Production as Probes of GPDs at Collider Energies
hep-ph.author: Zhuoyi Pang, Paweł Sznajder, Lech Szymanowski, Jakub Wagner
hep-ph.abstract: We study exclusive electroproduction of dijets in the collinear factorization framework as a probe of generalized parton distributions (GPDs). For quark dijet production, we extend previous analyses by including contributions from helicity GPDs and by assessing an additional leading-order electromagnetic channel governed by elastic nucleon form factors. Furthermore, we investigate exclusive gluon dijet production. We compare our prediction to HERA data and provide projections for measurements at the future Electron-Ion Collider.

hep-ph.title: Parametric Resonance of Higgsed Vector Dark Matter: Inflationary Initial Conditions and Sourced Displacements
hep-ph.author: Imtiaz Khan, Salvatore Capozziello, G. Mustafa, Niamat Ullah, Farruh Atamurotov
hep-ph.abstract: Parametric resonance in a Higgsed Abelian sector provides an efficient mechanism for producing vector dark matter, but its viability depends crucially on the origin of the initial dark-Higgs displacement that seeds the resonance. In this work, we investigate this initial-condition problem in a weakly coupled Abelian-Higgs theory with potential $V=\lambda_4(\phi^2-v^2)^2/4$, using the calibrated nonlinear broad-resonance relic map together with a stochastic inflationary analysis of the dark-Higgs condensate. We show that a minimal light-spectator realization fails under standard inflationary duration: while broad resonance and isocurvature constraints require \( \phi_0/H_I \gtrsim 3.3\times10^4, \) the stochastic equilibrium and finite-duration random walk produce only \( \phi/H_I=\mathcal O(1). \) This large displacement mismatch is robust against order-of-magnitude variations in the resonance efficiency and broadness threshold, establishing a model-independent obstruction to the stochastic branch. We then identify a distinct classically sourced branch, generated by a negative Hubble-induced mass, in which the condensate tracks a time-dependent minimum, \( \phi_0=\kappa H_*/\sqrt{\lambda_4}, \) and the radial fluctuation remains heavy during inflation. In this case, the fixed-$e/\lambda_D$ relic scaling shifts from \( m_X\propto \lambda_4^{5/8}H_I^{-3/2} \) to \( m_X\propto \kappa^{-3/2}\lambda_4 H_*^{-3/2}. \) We derive the simultaneous consistency conditions for this sourced branch, including broad resonance, adiabatic tracking, perturbativity, sub-Planckian displacement, thermal non-erasure, spectator backreaction, and control of inflationary vector fluctuations. Our results establish that Higgsed-vector resonance is not merely a dark-matter production mechanism, but a sensitive probe of the inflationary and reheating dynamics that determine its initial conditions.

hep-ph.title: Relativistic corrections and high-energy resummation for exclusive heavy quarkonium photoproduction
hep-ph.author: Maxim Nefedov
hep-ph.abstract: The $O(v^2)$ correction to the high-energy resummed coefficient function for the exclusive photoproduction of vector ($1^{--}$) heavy quarkonia off hadrons is computed, thereby taking into account corrections of $O(v^2 \alpha_s^n \ln^{n-1}(x/\xi))$. When expressed in terms of the physical vector-meson mass ($M_V$) and the relative heavy-quark velocity ($\langle v^2 \rangle$) using the Gremm-Kapustin relation, the computed correction turns out to be negligible at the scale $\mu_F=M_V$. However, it partially cancels the $\mu_F$ dependence of the $O(v^2)$ correction to the LO coefficient function in $\alpha_s$, thereby improving the robustness of the predictions.

hep-ph.title: Compositeness relations for near-threshold p-wave bound states
hep-ph.author: Guo-Ying Chen
hep-ph.abstract: We generalize Weinberg's compositeness relations to near-threshold p-wave bound states and derive the relations among the p-wave effective range expansion parameters, binding energy B, and the field renormalization constant Z. Unlike the s-wave case, the field renormalization constant Z for p-wave states depends on the renormalization scale. We obtain the renormalization equation for Z and provide its solution. We find that the negative-norm state reported more than a decade ago in p-wave sector can be avoided by an appropriate choice of the renormalization scale. We also present the general propagator for p-wave near-threshold states. Our results are expected to have broad applications in studying exotic states, as well as the structure of halo nuclei and Fashbach molecules.

hep-ph.title: Search for active-sterile neutrino transitions using Pierre Auger Observatory data
hep-ph.author: ThePierre Auger Collaboration:A. Abdul Halim, P. Abreu, M. Aglietta, M. Ahmed, I. Allekotte, K. Almeida Cheminant, R. Aloisio, J. Alvarez-Muñiz, A. Ambrosone, J. Ammerman Yebra, L. Anchordoqui, B. Andrada, L. Andrade Dourado, L. Apollonio, C. Aramo, J.C. Arteaga Velázquez, P. Assis, G. Avila, E. Avocone, A. Bakalova, Y. Balibrea, A. Baluta, F. Barbato, A. Bartz Mocellin, O. Batalla Cruz, J.P. Behler, C. Berat, M.E. Bertaina, M. Bianciotto, P.L. Biermann, V. Binet, K. Bismark, T. Bister, J. Biteau, J. Blazek, J. Blümer, M. Boháčová, D. Boncioli, C. Bonifazi, N. Borodai, J. Brack, P.G. Brichetto Orquera, S. Buitink, A. Bwembya, T.R. Caba Pineda, K.S. Caballero-Mora, S. Cabana-Freire, L. Caccianiga, J. Caraça-Valente, R. Caruso, A. Castellina, F. Catalani, G. Cataldi, L. Cazon, M. Cerda, B. Čermáková, A. Cermenati, K. Cerny, J.A. Chinellato, J. Chudoba, L. Chytka, R.W. Clay, A.C. Cobos Cerutti, R. Colalillo, R. Conceição, A. Condorelli, G. Consolati, M. Conte, F. Convenga, D. Correia dos Santos, P.J. Costa, C.E. Covault, M. Cristinziani, C.S. Cruz Sanchez, S. Dasso, K. Daumiller, B.R. Dawson, R.M. de Almeida, E.-T. de Boone, B. de Errico, J. de Jesús, S.J. de Jong, J.R.T. de Mello Neto, I. De Mitri, D. de Oliveira Franco, F. de Palma, V. de Souza, E. De Vito, A. Del Popolo, O. Deligny, N. Denner, K. Denner Syrokvas, L. Deval, A. di Matteo, C. Dobrigkeit, J.C. D'Olivo, L.M. Domingues Mendes, T. Dominguez, Y. Dominguez Ballesteros
hep-ph.abstract: We investigate the sensitivity of the Pierre Auger Observatory to physics beyond the Standard Model arising from magnetic-moment-induced transitions between active and heavy sterile neutrinos. Such dipole portal interactions can enhance neutrino-nucleon cross sections above a kinematic threshold set by the sterile neutrino mass, leading to observable modifications of neutrino detection rates at ultrahigh energies (UHE). We estimate the impact of these interactions on both down-going and Earth-skimming neutrino detection channels, the contrasting responses of which enable discrimination between an enhanced neutrino flux and a modified interaction cross section. Using the non-observation of UHE neutrino candidates, we derive neutrino-flux-dependent constraints with 90% confidence-level on the transition magnetic moment for sterile neutrino masses in the range 1 TeV-100 TeV. Under the assumed flux scenarios, the resulting flavor-independent limits extend existing bounds into previously unexplored parameter space.

hep-ph.title: High energy probes of Higgs self-coupling via $W$ boson fusion at future lepton colliders
hep-ph.author: Amir Subba, Hrishikesh Deka, Subhaditya Bhattacharya, Abhik Sarkar
hep-ph.abstract: We investigate the sensitivity to the Higgs self-coupling through $W$ boson fusion di-Higgs production at CLIC with a center-of-mass energy of $\sqrt{s}=3$~TeV. We study the interplay between the Higgs self-coupling modifier ($\kappa_{\lambda}$) and Higgs-gauge boson coupling modifiers ($\kappa_{V}$ and $\kappa_{2V}$) within the $\kappa$ framework. To enhance the separation between signal and background, we develop a graph neural network (GNN) based classifier that achieves a signal significance of $\mathscr{Z}\approx 20~\sigma$ at $5~\mathrm{ab}^{-1}$, substantially exceeding projected HL-LHC sensitivity. Our results demonstrate that high-energy lepton colliders, combined with graph-based machine learning, provide excellent sensitivity to the Higgs self-coupling and offer a powerful probe of new physics in the electroweak sector, potentially disentangling underlying SMEFT-like and HEFT-like structures.

hep-ph.title: Finite-Width Dissolution of Radial Spectroscopy in Single-Top Mesonic Correlations
hep-ph.author: Bing-Dong Wan, Shuo Yang
hep-ph.abstract: Within the heavy-mass expansion, the pole width of a system containing one unstable heavy constituent inherits the constituent width up to $\mathcal O(\Lambda_{\rm kin}^2/m_Q^2)$ corrections, while radial splittings remain $\mathcal O(\Lambda_{\rm rad})$. The top quark is an extreme realization of this hierarchy. We implement the complex top pole mass in an instantaneous Bethe--Salpeter framework, where a biorthogonal Hellmann--Feynman relation realizes width inheritance at the operator level and an artificial heavy-mass scan confirms the predicted $m_Q^{-2}$ suppression. The low-pole source-projected response has a single broad maximum at the physical top width in the $t\bar b$, $t\bar c$, and $t\bar u$ channels. Full width-dependent non-Hermitian re-diagonalization and a direct full-matrix resolvent evaluation confirm the progressive dissolution of the small-width radial maxima. Thus stable-top eigenvalues survive as reference poles but not as a resolvable multi-peak spectrum; they may instead leave qualitative, process-dependent $Wb\bar q$ signatures, such as a broad threshold enhancement or modified color flow.

hep-ph.title: On-shell renormalization in NREFT: a simplified description of resonances, bound states, and coupled channel effects
hep-ph.author: Guo-Ying Chen
hep-ph.abstract: We discuss several issues regarding the modern generalization of Weinberg's compositeness criterion. In particular, we demonstrate that the on-shell renormalization in NREFT reproduces Weinberg's result and provides a simple description of resonances, bound states, and coupled channel effects. Additionally, we present the complete propagator, including the charged channel for the near-threshold p-wave states.

hep-ph.title: Inverse-seesaw and inflationary scale relations in a supersymmetric 331 model from an SU(6) GUT model
hep-ph.author: Imtiaz Khan, Tianjun Li
hep-ph.abstract: We propose a $N=1$ supersymmetric $SU(6)$ theory with an intermediate $(SU(3)_C\times SU(3)_L\times U(1)_X)$ phase, in which common fields and operators relate the neutrinos, gauge mediation, unification, and symmetry-breaking sectors. The antisymmetric Dirac matrix of the inverse-seesaw sector has rank two, yielding one vanishing light-neutrino mass at leading order. A higher-dimensional symmetry-breaking correction lifts this zero mode through its projection onto the left and right null vectors of the Dirac matrix, leading to a quartic suppression in the ratio of the intermediate and ultraviolet scales. Complete unified messenger multiplets preserve the relative one-loop gauge coupling evolution while modifying the unified coupling. When the same supersymmetry-breaking spurion generates the singlet lepton-number-violating parameter, an analytical relation emerges between the messenger scale, the lepton-number mediator scale, and the unified coupling. The two-loop gauge evolution remains perturbative for the assumed heavy-threshold spectrum. In the inflationary sector, the scalar-amplitude normalization determines the coupling governing both the inflationary potential and the radial scalar mass in the broken vacuum. The physical scalar directions transverse to the inflaton are stable within the neutral supergravity subspace, while the combined inflationary and gauge-mediated conditions imply a significant sensitivity of the symmetry-breaking vacuum. An examination of the allowed operators shows that additional ultraviolet conditions are required to obtain the observed active-neutrino mixing, suppress competing lepton-number-violating terms, and complete the heavy-field spectrum. Our analysis establishes the analytical scale relations among the neutrino, messenger, unification, and inflationary sectors and identifies the conditions necessary for their simultaneous realization.

hep-ph.title: No Einstein Relation, No Problem: How Relativistic Weakly Coupled Heavy Quarks Equilibrate Beyond Leading Logarithm Anyway
hep-ph.author: Jean F. Du Plessis, Bruno Scheihing-Hitschfeld
hep-ph.abstract: Relativistic heavy quarks equilibrate even when their microscopic drag and momentum diffusion violate the Einstein relation. We investigate how equilibration proceeds as a function of the coupling and compared to simplified Fokker-Planck models. To do this, we present a detailed calculation of the momentum-transfer kernel in weakly coupled non-Abelian plasmas through strict $\mathcal{O}(g^4)$, and study the resulting dynamics at leading order in the inverse heavy-quark mass. Beyond leading logarithm, its non-Gaussian structure plays a crucial role in equilibration. We examine closely the analytic structure of the evolution kernel, determine the large-order asymptotics of the momentum-transfer cumulants, and show how the kernel's bounded analytic domain fixes asymmetric exponential tails at the level of the momentum transfer probability. Strongly coupled $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM also features an approximately Gaussian core and exponential tails, but differs in the nature of the kernel's singularities and the velocity dependence of the transport coefficients and tail exponents. These differences have distinct dynamical consequences: for the parameters studied, the persistence of the relativistic population in steeply falling spectra is largely explained by drag alone at very weak coupling, whereas fluctuation-induced survivor bias produces a large relative enhancement at strong coupling. Nevertheless, the shared qualitative structure between weak and strong coupling points the way towards a practical phenomenological description of heavy quarks anchored in first-principles field theory.

hep-ph.title: The decay $η_c\to p\bar pη$ with meson--baryon final-state interactions
hep-ph.author: Jing Song, Yu-Shan Ren, Eulogio Oset
hep-ph.abstract: We study the decay \(\eta_c\to p\bar{p}\eta\) by combining the SU(3) flavor structure of the primary production with final-state interactions in the \(p\eta\) and \(\bar{p}\eta\) subsystems, using the chiral unitary approach. The low-energy \(S_{11}\) dynamics, including the dynamically generated \(N^*(1535)\), is incorporated into the complete coupled-channel amplitude, and a phenomenological \(N^*(1895)\) contribution is included coherently. The \(p\eta\) and \(\bar{p}\eta\) invariant-mass distributions are well described, and the \(p\bar{p}\) distribution is predicted as a kinematic reflection of the \(\eta N\) dynamics. The results support the dynamical interpretation of the \(N^*(1535)\) and suggest possible additional \(S_{11}\) strength near \(1.9\)~GeV.

hep-ph.title: MadStree: automated evaluation of tree-level de Sitter correlators
hep-ph.author: Jiaqi Chen, Yi-Xiao Tao, Xinyi Wang, Dong Zhang
hep-ph.abstract: We first derived the formulae of recursive reduction and d log-form differential equations for arbitrary tree-level and loop-integrand cosmological correlators, taking the external relations of massless bulk propagators into consideration. The differential equations could be systematically solved and provide the efficient evaluation of them. We have implemented this methodology as a Mathematica package MadStree. To demonstrate the efficiency of our method, we evaluated up to $10^6$ points for each master integral in our examples, and found that the average computational cost per numerical point per master integral is on the order of $\mu\mathrm{s}$.

hep-ph.title: A universal probe of QCD spin physics from fragmentation energy correlator
hep-ph.author: Qing-Hong Cao, Xiaohui Liu, Zhite Yu, C.-P. Yuan, Feng Yuan, Shu-Tao Zhang, Hua Xing Zhu
hep-ph.abstract: We study the fragmentation energy correlator (FEC), which combines the nonperturbative fragmentation function with the infrared-safe energy correlator, as a new probe of the three-dimensional dynamics of QCD hadronization. We demonstrate, both theoretically and numerically, that FEC applies universally to inclusive hadron production in lepton-lepton, lepton-hadron, and hadron-hadron collisions, without requiring jet algorithms or simultaneous measurements of other heavy objects. Through the nontrivial transverse-spin dependence, FEC provides a sensitive probe of the chiral-symmetry-breaking scale in QCD via its variation with the energy-correlator scale.

hep-ph.title: Regression on high-dimensional phase space
hep-ph.author: Andrew J. Larkoski
hep-ph.abstract: Machine learning tasks in particle physics are typically expressed in terms of regression, or relaxation toward some optimal solution as defined by an objective or loss function. In this paper, we introduce a large multiplicity expansion for analyzing regression tasks, which enables significant analytic understanding. For concreteness, we study regression with energy flow polynomials (EFPs), a complete linear basis of infrared and collinear safe observables on Lorentz invariant phase space. While the expectation value of any EFP scales like a constant in the large multiplicity limit, we prove that the covariance on uniform phase space of any two EFPs is highly suppressed and scales like the inverse of the squared multiplicity. This very unintuitive result relies on detailed cancellation guaranteed by the interplay of permutation invariance, momentum conservation, and rotational invariance. This scaling of the covariance with multiplicity further implies that the coefficients in an expansion of EFPs must scale quadratically in multiplicity. We present an example of regression with EFPs as applied to $e^+e^-\to$ hadrons events, and show how the regression can be solved analytically through the complementary expansions of the large multiplicity limit and of familiar fixed-order perturbation theory of QCD.

hep-ph.title: Two-peak gravitational wave spectra from supercooled two-field phase transitions
hep-ph.author: Daniel Araújo, João Gonçalves, Danny Marfatia
hep-ph.abstract: We study the gravitational wave (GW) spectrum generated by supercooled first-order phase transitions in two-field conformal models. We construct three representative toy models that capture the essential features of these models, derive analytical criteria for the existence of two-step transitions, and show how the two-field dynamics generate a genuine two-peak GW spectrum. We identify regions of parameter space in which two-peak GW spectra are observable at LISA and the Einstein Telescope. By way of illustration, we apply our analysis to a realistic conformal dark SU(3) model.

hep-ph.title: Electromagnetic Structure of $Ω_{ccc}^{++}$ and $Ω_{bbb}^{-}$ baryons from a covariant three-body Faddeev equation
hep-ph.author: Zhao-Qian Yao
hep-ph.abstract: We investigate the electromagnetic structure of the ground-state $\Omega_{ccc}^{++}$ and $\Omega_{bbb}^{-}$ baryons using a Poincaré-covariant three-body Faddeev equation within the rainbow--ladder truncation. We calculate the complete set of elastic spin-$3/2$ multipole form factors, $G_{E0}$, $G_{M1}$, $G_{E2}$, and $G_{M3}$. The leading electric and magnetic form factors become markedly harder from the charm to the bottom sector, revealing the substantially more compact electromagnetic structure of the $\Omega_{bbb}^{-}$. For $\Omega_{ccc}^{++}$, the electric form factor and charge radius at low momentum transfer agree well with the available lQCD results. From the magnetic-dipole form factor at zero momentum transfer, $G_{M1}(0)$, we obtain the magnetic moments $\mu_{\Omega_{ccc}^{++}}=1.26\,\mu_N$ and $\mu_{\Omega_{bbb}^{-}}=-0.207\,\mu_N$. For $G_{E2}$ and $G_{M3}$, the electric-quadrupole structure exhibits a stronger charm-to-bottom evolution than the charge-normalized magnetic-octupole structure. Finally, comparison of the charm and bottom systems shows that both $G_{M1}(0)$ and the relation between the electric and magnetic radii move closer to their leading nonrelativistic heavy-quark expectations as the quark mass increases.

hep-ph.title: Thermal Krylov complexity and entropy of inflationary modes with different comoving-wavenumber dependences
hep-ph.author: Tao Li, Lei-Hua Liu
hep-ph.abstract: We study thermal Krylov complexity and Krylov entropy for primordial scalar modes in three inflationary models with different comoving-wavenumber dependences. These models are canonical single-field inflation, a non-trivial sound speed model, and a modified dispersion relation model. We construct a purified two-mode thermal state and first study its unitary Krylov evolution in an ideal closed system. In the parameter range considered here, the sound-speed correction increases the mean values and oscillation amplitudes of the Krylov quantities. The modified dispersion relation produces a stage-dependent oscillatory structure. We then introduce an independent effective open-system parametrization. The normalized Krylov distribution is controlled by a geometric ratio that combines thermal occupation, coherent spreading, and effective attenuation. We derive explicit expressions for Krylov complexity and Krylov entropy. We also obtain their low- and high-temperature limits. The sound-speed correction enhances the geometric ratio in the adopted parameter range. For the modified dispersion relation, coherent spreading and effective attenuation compete. These results show how thermal occupation and modified mode frequencies control Krylov-space spreading in the three inflationary models.

hep-ph.title: CANTON-$μ$ Proposal: A Next-Generation Muon $g-2$ Measurement at Sub-0.1 ppm Precision
hep-ph.author: Ce Zhang, Yu Xu, On Kim, Bingzhi Li, Zejia Lu, Saskia Charity, Guodong Shen, Liangwen Chen, Fedor Ignatov, Liang Li, Qiang Li, Xueheng Zhang, Zhiyu Sun
hep-ph.abstract: We propose a next-generation precision measurement of the muon anomalous magnetic moment (muon g-2) at the High Intensity Heavy-Ion Accelerator Facility (HIAF) in Huizhou, China. We refer to this proposed experimental programme as CANTON-$\mu$ (Coherent Anomalous magNetic momenT ObservatioN with muon). HIAF's intense, pulsed GeV-scale muon beams, particularly for negative muons, provide a promising basis for this programme. Building on two previously proposed storage-ring concepts, this work develops HIAF-specific experimental schemes that relax the conventional magic-momentum constraint and allow greater flexibility in the choice of beam momentum. We assess the expected muon intensity at HIAF and the corresponding statistical sensitivity. For each scheme, we identify its distinctive systematic effects, examine feasible control strategies, and propose quantitative systematic-uncertainty targets. Together, the statistical projections and systematic-uncertainty targets indicate prospective total precisions of 0.1 ppm in Phase-I, comparable to the current Fermilab precision, with the potential to reach the 0.05 ppm level in Phase-II following the planned HIAF upgrade. At the ultimate projected precision, the measurement would provide a stringent test of the Standard Model and probe new physics at multi-TeV scales. A focus on negative-muon measurements would enable direct comparison with existing high-precision positive-muon results and strengthen tests of CPT symmetry in the muon sector within the Standard-Model Extension, with a projected sensitivity at the $10^{-24}$ GeV level, an order of magnitude beyond current limits.

hep-ph.title: Hall Viscosity in the Quark-Gluon Plasma
hep-ph.author: Sukrut Mondkar, Giorgio Torrieri, Matthias Kaminski, René Meyer
hep-ph.abstract: We study the Hall viscosity of the quark gluon plasma (QGP) created in non-central heavy-ion collisions. In the presence of a strong magnetic field or vorticity, rotational symmetry is broken from $O(3)$ to $O(2)$, allowing for two independent Hall viscosities associated with shear deformations transverse and parallel to the symmetry-breaking direction. We find the corresponding constitutive relations by extending the kinetic-theory mechanism to three spatial dimensions and provide parametric estimates of the Hall viscosities under realistic QGP conditions. Both kinetic-theory and holographic estimates indicate that Hall viscosities are comparable in magnitude to the shear viscosity at zero magnetic field. We further show that Hall viscous stresses at hydrodynamic initialization can be as large as standard viscous corrections and identify observable consequences in flow and event-plane correlations.

hep-ph.title: It Just Takes Two: Scaling Amortized Inference to Large Sets
hep-ph.author: Antoine Wehenkel, Michael Kagan, Lukas Heinrich, Chris Pollard
hep-ph.abstract: Neural posterior estimation has emerged as a powerful tool for amortized inference, with growing adoption across scientific and applied domains. In many of these applications, the conditioning variable is a set of observations whose elements depend not only on the target but also on unknown factors shared across the set. Optimal inference therefore requires treating the set jointly, which in turn requires training the estimator at the deployment set size -- a regime where memory and compute quickly become prohibitive. We introduce a simple, theoretically grounded strategy that decouples representation learning from posterior modeling. Our method trains a mean-pool Deep Set on sets of size at most two, producing an encoder that generalizes to arbitrary set sizes. The inference head is then finetuned on pre-aggregated embeddings, making training cost essentially independent of the deployment set size N. Across scalar, image, multi-view 3D, molecular, and high-dimensional conditional generation benchmarks with N in the thousands, our approach matches or outperforms standard baselines at a fraction of the compute.

hep-ph.title: Neutron stars with an agnostic Dark sector: Core and Halo configurations from a two-fluid approach
hep-ph.author: Asit karan, Tuhin Malik, Asim Kumar Saha, Constança Providência, Ritam Mallick
hep-ph.abstract: The study of dark matter admixed neutron stars has the potential to advance our understanding of dark matter particle candidates. However, the large parameter space of dark matter particle masses restricts a systematic, model-independent study. In this analysis, we employ agnostic hadronic and dark-matter equations of state to construct dark-matter-admixed neutron stars within a two-fluid formalism. Dark matter is characterized solely by its low-density equation of state and mass and is modeled as a Fermi gas, while hadronic matter is anchored at low and high densities by chiral effective field theory and perturbative quantum chromodynamics calculations. A speed-of-sound parametrization describes the intermediate- and high-density regimes of both hadronic and dark matter, enabling an agnostic treatment of the dark matter equation of state that is constrained only by thermodynamic consistency and does not favor softer or stiffer behavior. Within this agnostic framework, we find that dark matter does not generically compactify the star: light dark matter forms extended halos that raise the tidal deformability, while heavy dark matter forms compact cores that lower it. Consequently, the dominant observational constraint shifts from gravitational-wave tidal deformability for light, halo-dominated models to NICER mass-radius data for heavy, core-dominated models. Using current data at $1\sigma$, we constrain the dark matter fraction to $f_{\mathrm{DM}} \lesssim 0.11$ for light dark matter. By treating the medium- and high-density dark matter equation of state agnostically within a fermionic framework, our approach yields conservative and broadly applicable bounds on the dark matter content of neutron stars. Neutron stars with similar masses but very different tidal deformabilities could be a smoking-gun signature of dark matter in neutron stars.

hep-ph.title: Background-independent one-loop renormalization of tensor and scalar primordial spectra
hep-ph.author: Guillermo Ballesteros, Jesús Gambín Egea, Flavio Riccardi
hep-ph.abstract: We present a background-independent renormalization framework for one-loop primordial spectra. We apply it to two observables: the scalar-induced tensor spectrum sourced by a minimally coupled spectator field, and the scalar spectrum generated by potential self-interactions. In both cases, the UV part of the loops is isolated and, using the universal WKB behavior of the internal modes, the UV poles are extracted analytically and absorbed into local counterterms without having to specify either the background evolution or the full dynamics of the field running in the loop. This yields finite model-independent expressions for the renormalized spectra amenable to numerical analysis.

hep-ph.title: Perusing confining pseudoreal theories: hints of emerging massless spin-1 bosons
hep-ph.author: Giacomo Cacciapaglia, Konstantinos Kollias
hep-ph.abstract: Solving quantum field theory, which is at the basis of the standard model of particle interactions, is one of the main tasks of contemporary theoretical physics. Minimal asymptotically free pseudoreal theories, containing one or two species of massless Weyl fermions in pseudoreal representations of the gauge group, flow towards a poorly understood infrared dynamics. We provide a comprehensive study of all non-supersymmetric pseudoreal theories, first identifying the ones that likely flow towards a conformal dynamics. Assuming that the remaining ones confine, we find that tumbling hints the possible formation of a non-trivial condensate dynamics, consistently with other symmetry considerations. All but one one-species theories may feature at least one massless spin-1 state. Instead, the only confining two-species theory likely features two massless spin-1 states and one Nambu-Goldstone boson. These expectations must be further tested, for instance by use of Lattice simulations, the functional renormalization group, and supersymmetric analogs.

hep-ph.title: Gravitational Waves from Multiple Cosmic Superstrings and the Overshoot Problem
hep-ph.author: Luca Brunelli, Michele Cicoli, Muhammad Hassan, Seyed Ehsan Qoreishi, Francisco Gil Pedro
hep-ph.abstract: Post inflationary string cosmology can feature an initial population of multiple species of cosmic superstrings whose tension is controlled by a modulus rolling over a steep potential toward a late-time minimum. We perform a full analysis of the associated dynamical system, finding that overshooting the minimum is prevented by the friction of a radiation background of gravitational waves produced from the early decay of effective strings arising from NS5- and D3-branes wrapped around internal cycles. On the other hand, fundamental strings survive longer and decay when the modulus is oscillating around the minimum and they have about $1/3$ of the total energy density. The spectrum of gravitational waves generated by the decays of these multiple cosmic superstrings, even if diluted by a late epoch of modulus domination, can still result in a high-frequency, multi-peaked signal, offering an observational signature of generic features of string theory.

hep-ph.title: Density-induced dark-baryon conversion in $Δ-$admixed hypernuclear neutron stars
hep-ph.author: Niyar Prabhat Kalita, Vivek Baruah Thapa, Bhanu Prakash Pant, Anil Kumar, Partha Konar
hep-ph.abstract: We investigate density-induced conversion of neutrons into a neutral dark baryon $\chi$ in cold, charge-neutral, $\beta$-equilibrated neutron-star matter containing hyperons and all $\Delta(1232)$ quartet. The hadronic sector is modeled within a density-dependent covariant density-functional framework using the DDME2 parametrization. A scalar Higgs portal is included as a possible interaction channel between the visible and dark sectors, although its mean-field contribution is negligible for the couplings adopted here. Unlike fixed dark-matter admixture models or scenarios in which nucleon-to-DM conversion is driven by Higgs exchange, the $\chi$ abundance is determined self-consistently from chemical equilibrium and baryon-number conservation. We find that hyperons and $\Delta$ resonances alter the neutron chemical potential, delay the onset of $\chi$, and suppress its abundance relative to nucleonic matter. This competition induces characteristic changes in the equation of state, particle fractions, sound speed, and adiabatic index. For $m_\chi=1250$, $1300$, and $1400$ MeV, the maximum masses of the complete $N+Y+\Delta+\chi$ configurations are $1.806$, $1.899$ and $2.024,M_\odot$, respectively, indicating that the massive-pulsar constraint disfavors the lighter dark-baryon benchmarks. The radial profiles further show that for $m_\chi=1400$ MeV, $\chi$ is confined to the inner core of the most massive stars, while canonical configurations remain essentially unaffected. Thus, the stellar modifications arise primarily from conversion-induced rearrangement of the equilibrium composition rather than from Higgs-mediated interactions. These results highlight the importance of treating conventional non-nucleonic degrees of freedom and density-generated dark baryons on an equal footing when assessing the astrophysical viability of dark-sector extensions of dense matter.

hep-ph.title: Cosmological Collider Signals From a Triangle Loop
hep-ph.author: Zhehan Qin, Zhong-Zhi Xianyu
hep-ph.abstract: Triangular loop signals appear frequently in cosmological collider models but their analytical forms remain unknown due to multiple technical challenges. Here, we determine for the first time the leading analytical cosmological collider signals generated by a massive scalar triangle loop in inflationary bispectrum and trispectrum. Combining a directional cutting rule with partial Mellin-Barnes representations, we obtain both the local and nonlocal trispectrum signals in a soft limit and derive the leading signal in the squeezed bispectrum. Remarkably, all these signals are reproduced by the corresponding bubble diagram with a single effective pinched coupling. Signals beyond leading order and cases with arbitrary internal masses, spins, and interactions can be generated within the same framework. Our approach also provides a systematic route to extracting analytical loop signals from general cosmological correlators.

hep-ph.title: Luminosity Signatures of Dark Sector Particles from Black Hole Evaporation in Neutron Stars
hep-ph.author: Ioannis Dalianis, Anastasios Irakleous
hep-ph.abstract: Microscopic black holes may form at the centers of neutron stars through the accumulation and collapse of dark matter. While Standard Model particles produced by Hawking evaporation are efficiently absorbed by the dense stellar medium, sufficiently weakly interacting and long-lived particles can escape and subsequently decay into high-energy neutrinos, photons, or charged particles, providing an indirect probe of Hawking radiation. We examine the joint energy--angular distribution of these secondary particles, incorporating mediator propagation, energy-dependent decay, and relativistic decay kinematics. For relativistic mediators, the normalized energy-integrated angular profile becomes approximately independent of the black hole temperature, with its characteristic extent controlled primarily by the combination $c\tau_S/D$ of the mediator lifetime and source distance, as the boost enhancement of the decay length is compensated by relativistic beaming. We demonstrate the viability of this mechanism and illustrate its phenomenology with gravitationally coupled scalars, axion-like particles (ALPs), dark photons, and heavy neutral leptons. Comparing with monochromatic mediator production from dark matter annihilation, we find that the energy-integrated angular profiles can be nearly degenerate, while the energy spectra and energy-resolved angular distributions remain distinct. Although the predicted signals may lie beyond the reach of current observatories, these complementary spectral and angular signatures provide potential targets for future high-energy neutrino and gamma-ray searches.

hep-ph.title: Self-Interacting Dark Matter: From Particle Physics Theories to Structure Formation Simulations
