hep-th.author: Srijan Kumar
hep-th.abstract: We study the singlet sector of large-$N$, $O(N)$ vector model on $S^1_\beta\times S^2_r$ in presence of an angular potential $\Omega$. We compute the free energy of the model both at the free fixed point as well as the non-trivial fixed point. The model undergoes a phase transition when the temperature $T$ and angular potential attain the relation $T^2r^2\sim N (1-\omega^2)$, where $\omega=r\Omega$ and $r$ is the radius of $S^2$, with $Tr\gg1$, at both the fixed points, with different numerical coefficients. The transition was studied earlier at zero angular potential at $Tr\sim \sqrt{N}$. The holonomy eigenvalue distribution, having support on the full circle below the transition, develops a gap above it, called the Gross-Witten-Wadia transition. The angular potential introduces an additional parameter to such a transition, tuning it, the transition can occur even at a fixed temperature. We show that for the free model transition can occur as $1-\omega^2\sim 1/N$ while $Tr\sim O(1)$. For the interacting model the computation is performed at a limit $Tr\gg1$, thus we show the same at a large but fixed temperature which does not scale as $\sqrt{N}$. In the ungapped phase, the free energy exhibits a double pole near $\omega^2=1$ for both the fixed points. This is possibly due to the fact that the theory projected onto the singlets is non-local and therefore need not obey the leading simple pole scaling of a local thermal effective action.

hep-th.title: $q$-deformed Weil-Petersson volumes from the spectral edge of DSSYK and supersymmetric extensions
hep-th.author: Wasif Ahmed, Joydeep Naskar, Krishan Saraswat
hep-th.abstract: The $q$-deformed Weil-Petersson volumes of Do and Norbury are the top-degree parts of Okuyama's discrete volumes, which are defined by topological recursion on the spectral curve of the double-scaled SYK (DSSYK) model. We show that the same $q$-deformed volumes can also be obtained from a double-scaled matrix model whose disk density is found by zooming in on the soft edges of the DSSYK density. Applying the same procedure to the hard edge of $\mathcal{N}=1$ DSSYK, we obtain candidate $q$-deformed $\mathcal{N}=1$ super Weil-Petersson volumes. They are polynomials of fixed degree, and they reduce to $\mathcal{N}=1$ super Weil-Petersson volumes in a scaled $q\to1$ limit. These candidate volumes differ from the $\mathcal{N}=1$ volumes of Do and Norbury in (arXiv:2510.12431) up to what we call ``irrelevant'' contributions which exactly vanish in the scaled $q\to 1$ limit. Together, these results demonstrate how $q$-deformed volumes can be naturally associated to the spectral edges of various DSSYK models and provides an intuitive way to construct them in supersymmetric contexts.

hep-th.title: Modular Flow and Holographic Timelike Entanglement Entropy in AdS and Flat Holography
hep-th.author: Mehdi Hakami Shalamzari, Zahra Paygozar, Mahdi Kord Zangeneh
hep-th.abstract: Timelike entanglement entropy provides a useful probe of holographic theories, yet an explicit bulk realization of the modular flow underlying its timelike extremal curve construction has so far been lacking. We construct modular flows associated with spacelike and timelike intervals in AdS$_{3}$/CFT$_{2}$ and extend this framework to flat$_{3}$/CCFT$_{2}$. Beginning with the boundary symmetry generators, we explicitly derive the boundary modular flows and extend them into the bulk, providing a systematic procedure that relates bulk modular flows to the extremal curves and holographic (timelike) entanglement entropy. For spacelike intervals, the resulting bulk modular flows determine the extremal curves, whose integrated line elements reproduce the standard holographic entanglement entropy. We then generalize this approach to timelike intervals, explicitly constructing the modular flows whose fixed points reproduce the extremal spacelike and timelike curves, which give the holographic timelike entanglement entropy. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first explicit construction of the modular flow associated with a timelike extremal curve for a timelike interval. The same procedure is then carried over to flat$_{3}$/CCFT$_{2}$, which gives rise to the holographic (timelike) entanglement entropy. Finally, we show that the flat space results obtained in this work can be recovered from their AdS$_3$ counterparts in the flat space limit.

hep-th.title: Holographic Pseudo Entropy from the Rindler Method in AdS and Flat Space
hep-th.author: Mehdi Hakami Shalamzari, Zahra Paygozar, Mahdi Kord Zangeneh
hep-th.abstract: Via the Rindler method, we study holographic timelike entanglement entropy (TEE) for a general timelike interval in AdS$_3$/CFT$_2$ and flat$_3$/CCFT$_2$. The TEE is the pseudo entropy of a timelike interval. In the bulk, the imaginary part of the TEE comes from a timelike geodesic. After a Rindler transformation to a rotating BTZ black hole, the two spacelike extremal curves lie on the inner and outer horizons, and exchanging $l_u\leftrightarrow \ell l_\phi$ takes one to the other. We clarify the geometric role of the timelike extremal curve in the Rindler frame. We show that it is the line $\tilde U=\tilde V=0$ stretched between the two horizons, starting on the inner horizon, touching the outer horizon at its midpoint, and returning to the inner one. No such curve exists outside the region between the horizons. Its length, $i\pi\ell$, is independent of the interval, and it alone produces the imaginary part $i\pi c/6$. We follow the same procedure in flat space holography, where the spacelike curve sits on the cosmological horizon and the timelike curve lies between the cosmological horizon and timelike infinity. Evaluating the holographic TEE for a timelike interval in CCFT$_2$ on the plane, we find that, in contrast with the cylinder, the real and imaginary parts are equal.

hep-th.title: Post-Newtonian theory in de Sitter and anti-de Sitter spacetimes
hep-th.author: R. Loganayagam, Avi Wadhwa
hep-th.abstract: We develop the post-Newtonian framework for the near-zone dynamics of a binary in de Sitter and anti-de Sitter spacetime. We consider a binary interacting via a free scalar field in a fixed (A)dS background in $D+1$ spacetime dimensions, with $D\ge3$ and odd. Using a novel multipole re-summation technique, we solve for the field degrees of freedom to obtain an effective particle description in the form of a Fokker action. We derive the equations of motion for the binary up to second post-Newtonian (2PN) order, and obtain the corresponding 2PN Hamiltonian and conserved charges in phase space. We show that the conformal algebra, corresponding to the isometry algebra of the (A)dS background, is realised in phase space as a curvature-dependent deformation of the Poincare algebra at each PN order. This serves as a non-trivial check on our results. Our results provide a systematic extension of post-Newtonian effective dynamics to finite-curvature backgrounds. This could serve as a useful framework for studying bound-state dynamics in (A)dS as well as in the corresponding holographic CFT.

hep-th.title: All Order Gravitational Wave Tails from Classical Soft Theorem for Subleading Post-Newtonian Expansion
hep-th.author: Debanjan Karan, Babli Khatun
hep-th.abstract: The low-frequency gravitational waveform emitted in a classical scattering process contains an infinite tower of late- and early-time tail terms of the form $u^{-r}(\ln|u|)^{r-1}$, $r \geq 1$. In the Newtonian limit, the coefficients of this entire tower have recently been shown to be universal, i.e. fixed by the asymptotic data of the scattering objects alone. At the retained order in the velocity expansion, these leading-logarithmic tails are determined to all orders in Newton's constant $G$. We extend this result to the first subleading order in the post-Newtonian expansion of the asymptotic states. We consider scattering of an arbitrary number of incoming and outgoing nonrelativistic objects interacting only through gravity at long range, and we derive the complete tower of tail terms at this order. The correction arises from the first subleading term in the retardation expansion and is determined by the asymptotic Newtonian trajectories of the massive particles. Its coefficients are again determined entirely by the asymptotic trajectories and are independent of the details of the interaction. For $2\to2$ scattering, the leading-logarithmic series can be summed in closed form. Our results agree with a relativistic conjecture proposed in earlier workarXiv:2610.07134.

hep-th.title: Boundary preparation of strong Mpemba states in holography
hep-th.author: Yu Shi, Xinwu Liu, Liping Li, Chikun Ding, Yuebing Zhou, Changqing Liu, Sheng Long
hep-th.abstract: We study the boundary preparation of strong Mpemba states in a probe Abelian Higgs model on a fixed AdS black brane. Different drives ending at the same charge density can prepare states with different slow mode amplitudes. Two pulses cancel the slowest mode at linear order, but charge exchange during preparation and radial Maxwell feedback regenerate a slow tail at cubic order. We derive the complete cubic response from the lower order field equations, including feedback after source removal, and use it to predict a compensating pulse. Full nonlinear evolution confirms that the compensation reduces the residual slow amplitude from third to fifth order in the source strength. For a representative protocol, the slow amplitude is reduced by a factor of about 600 relative to linear cancellation. This extends the fast relaxation window without changing the final quasinormal mode spectrum. Further nonlinear tuning suppresses the estimated residual amplitude to the level of numerical resolution. The prepared states can overtake a weakly driven reference despite having a larger excess free energy at source removal. Three pulses also suppress a second slow channel over the resolved time window and reveal interference between faster modes. Starting from a common initial state, controls with zero net charge transfer reach a given relaxation threshold sooner than passive relaxation, even when the full control duration is included.

hep-th.title: Mapping AdS$_4$ quantum gravity via the Bethe Ansatz formula
hep-th.author: Cheng Peng, Xuao Zhang, Ziruo Zhang
hep-th.abstract: The topologically twisted index of 3d ADHM theory can be written as a sum over solutions to the Bethe Ansatz Equations (BAEs) of the XXZ-type model constructed from quantum toroidal $\mathfrak{gl}_1$. Via a novel numerical algorithm, we solve for all $p(N)$ physical solutions at $N\leq 21$, where $p(N)$ denotes the number of partitions of $N$. Surveying these solutions, we find that in addition to the known "1-cut" solution dual to dyonic black holes, where the gauge holonomies are distributed along a single curve in the complex plane, there are "dressed" 1-cut solutions dual to combined configurations of the black hole and M2-branes, $m$-cut solutions dual to $\mathbb{Z}_m$ orbifolds of the black hole, a discrete family of solutions interpolating between the 1-cut and 3-cut solutions whose bulk dual is not yet identified, together with other exotic solutions, at each value of $N$. We show that the $1,2,3$-cut solutions and interpolating solutions all have a well-defined large $N$ limit, and analytically compute their leading order distribution of gauge holonomies. Whenever possible, we fit the contributions of the solutions to the index to all orders in the $1/N$ expansion with high-precision numerics, and extract the leading non-perturbative correction. With exceptions, these are matched with the results of equivariant localization in the bulk, and the action of wrapped M2-branes respectively.

hep-th.title: Beyond the Fock Vacuum in Finite-$N$ Bilocal Algebras of Vector Models
hep-th.author: Byoungjoon Ahn, Robert de Mello Koch, Vatsal Garg, Antal Jevicki, Junggi Yoon
hep-th.abstract: We discuss the finite-$N$ Hilbert space of bilocal operators that underlies bilocal holography of vector models, beyond the sector built on the Fock vacuum. If the microscopic oscillator Fock space carries a multiplicity-free dual action of a compact color group $G$ and a bilocal algebra, Howe duality implies that projection to the derived subgroup $[G,G]$ selects precisely the characters of the abelianization $G^{\rm ab}=G/[G,G]$ that occur in the Fock space. Thus $O(N)/SO(N)=\mathbb Z_2$ gives two sectors, $U(N)/SU(N)=U(1)$ gives integer determinant-charge sectors, while $Sp(N)$ is perfect and gives no additional sector; Bose/Fermi statistics and the number of modes determine which sectors are actually realized. We construct the epsilon and determinant backgrounds that generate these sectors, together with their finite-$N$ constraints and Casimirs, and find that the two bosonic $O(N)$ sectors are not distinguished by any Casimir. Using group-integral projectors, we derive explicit sector-resolved characters for the $O(N)$ and $U(N)$ theories. Around each new background we solve the constraints with auxiliary oscillators, which form a Fermi sea for bosonic matter. In the free vector model on $\mathbb R\times S^2$ the lowest states in the new sectors are baryonic primaries; we determine their energies, degeneracies and spin content exactly at finite $N$, together with their lowest energy at fixed angular momentum.

hep-th.title: Exact holographic superfluid at the Bogomolny point: transport, large charge, and Rényi entropies
hep-th.author: Siqing Yu
hep-th.abstract: The probe-limit Abelian Higgs model in AdS$_5$ is a standard holographic model of a strongly coupled superfluid, usually solved numerically. With the scalar mass at the Breitenlohner-Freedman bound and the quartic coupling at the Bogomolny value, its condensed phase has a closed form on every static, uncharged AdS$_5$ background with maximally symmetric spatial sections. We prove that it is the global minimum of the free energy at fixed charge, and linearly stable, as is any nodeless condensate of the model in standard quantization with nonnegative quartic coupling and no superflow. On the planar black brane it is the superfluid at all temperatures below $T_c$: the superfluid fraction follows the Gorter-Casimir two-fluid law exactly, and the speed and attenuation of sound are in closed form. In global AdS$_5$ it is the lowest state of charge $Q$ on $\mathbb{R}\times S^3$ within the model, with its scaling dimension in closed form at all $Q$, classically in the bulk. Its excitations include towers, from an infrared fixed point of the probe sector, that the superfluid effective theory does not describe. On the hyperbolic black holes that compute charged Rényi entropies of a ball, it is a homogeneous hairy phase whose condensate does not fall off toward the entangling surface. With a pinning field there, the phase sets in at Rényi index exactly one at zero chemical potential, as found for a neutral scalar. Well below a bound on the quartic coupling, the static, homogeneous solutions computed at other couplings and masses keep an infrared fixed point with towers, but not the exact two-fluid law.

hep-th.title: The running of Weyl gauged gravity: asymptotic freedom, its obstruction, and a way out
hep-th.author: Diego Buccio, Fabrizio Chicconi, Luca Parente, Omar Zanusso
hep-th.abstract: We compute the one-loop beta functions of quadratic gravity in Weyl conformal geometry, the gauge theory of diffeomorphisms and dilatations with a dynamical Weyl gauge boson. The divergences are extracted diagrammatically in the background field method, with a gauge fixing procedure adapted to the semidirect product structure of the gauge group. The Weyl-tensor coupling and the Weyl gauge coupling are asymptotically free, and the running of the latter is special, being independent of the other couplings and of any two-derivative matter content. The obstruction to an ultraviolet completion comes from the square of a Weyl-covariant curvature scalar, denoted $\widehat{R}{}^2$: the flow of the corresponding coupling has no fixed point in the physically interesting region and becomes trivial, the only real fixed points require a decoupled Weyl boson and a tachyonic scalar mode. This also holds when including the Standard Model with any nonminimal Higgs coupling and, more generally, for any matter with two-derivative kinetic terms. Weyl-invariant four-derivative scalars with a sufficiently large coupling to $\widehat{R}{}^2$ can remove the obstruction, producing a fixed point in the physical region that is ultraviolet attractive in all directions and has a nonvanishing Weyl gauge coupling.

hep-th.title: A Common Type II Origin of Galilean and Carroll Superstrings
hep-th.author: Mehmet Ozkan, Utku Zorba
hep-th.abstract: We show that the relativistic Type-II superalgebras, once the fundamental-string winding charge is retained alongside the momentum, admit a single non-Lorentzian contraction with two invariant translation ideals, whose complementary quotients yield Galilean and magnetic-Carroll superalgebras. The complementary vector charge required for this structure is thus intrinsic to string theory. The IIA realization is particle-like and the IIB realization string-like, a distinction fixed by chirality, and spacelike T-duality relates the two while preserving each non-Lorentzian structure. The same contraction is finite on the doubled Green--Schwarz action, including all fermion terms and local kappa symmetry, where the two supersymmetries appear as the two polarizations of a single worldsheet theory. These results unify two distinct non-Lorentzian corners of string theory within a common Type-II origin and open a route toward a broader web of non-Lorentzian dualities and possible holographic generalizations.

hep-th.title: Transgression branes in seven dimensions
hep-th.author: Pablo Mora(CURE, Universidad de la República, Uruguay)
hep-th.abstract: A seven dimensional theory with branes, described by a Transgression Action is investigated. The theory has special properties owing to the factorization of the trace used to define the Transgression form. It is shown that in some cases the theory is similar to the models of branes proposed by Nepomechie, Wu and Zee as a higher dimensional generalization of models of particles with fractional statistics of Wilczek, Wu and Zee. Static Euclidean solutions are presented, and compared with similar solutions of Nepomechie,Wu and Zee. Then Lorentzian static solutions are considered, based in solutions of constant curvature black holes presented by Bañados and further studied by Guilleminot, Olea and Petrov. Topological phases and their implications for quantum statistics are discussed.

hep-th.title: Symmetry breaking from conformality loss on holographic Rényi defects
hep-th.author: Siqing Yu
hep-th.abstract: The Rényi entropies of a ball are computed by the Rényi defect (the twist operator viewed as a conformal defect), which in holography is dual to a hyperbolic black hole. We identify hyperbolic black holes with homogeneous charged scalar hair as conformal defects that break the U(1) symmetry. At large $N$ and for repulsive self-interactions, conformality loss of the Rényi defect turns explicit symmetry breaking into spontaneous breaking: below a critical index $n_*$ the symmetry-breaking defect is reached only with an explicit source on the entangling surface; at $n_*$ the dimension of a defect operator from a light charged scalar turns complex; beyond $n_*$ the Rényi defect flows to the symmetry-breaking defect with no source. The condensate, expected to break the symmetries of hyperbolic space, instead preserves them outside a layer at the entangling surface, whose width diverges at $n_*$ with Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless scaling. The universal term of the Rényi entropy therefore jumps at $n_*$ to that of the symmetry-breaking defect. We demonstrate this mechanism in the probe Abelian Higgs model in AdS$_5$ at the Bogomolny point, with closed-form saddles and defect data, and numerical flows. For a ball we prove that a positive source-free flow exists exactly when $n>n_*$ and the radius is large enough, and that it ends at the symmetry-breaking defect as the radius grows.

hep-th.title: Explicit Symmetry Breaking in Non-Abelian Scalar Theories and One-Loop Renormalization
hep-th.author: Lucas Ducastelo de C. C. Lima
hep-th.abstract: We investigate the one-loop renormalization of a Yang--Mills--Faddeev--Popov theory deformed by a complex scalar doublet with explicitly broken $SU(2)$ gauge symmetry. At the classical level, we map the complex doublet into a real $SO(4)$ multiplet and discuss its generalization to $SU(N)$ through $SO(2N)$. The symmetry breaking is introduced by splitting the scalar masses and quartic couplings. Using the background field method and the Schwinger--DeWitt technique, we compute the one-loop divergences and establish renormalizability at this order. We derive the beta functions, recovering the known gauge-invariant limit, and analyze the RG flow. Although the Yang--Mills coupling remains asymptotically free, the rescaled quartic couplings have no real fixed points, and the one-loop flow develops a divergence at a finite energy scale, even in the symmetric limit. The asymmetry between the rescaled scalar self-couplings increases toward the UV and decreases toward the IR, within the region of nonnegative scalar self-couplings.

hep-th.title: Effect of ultralight dark matter on compact binary mergers
hep-th.author: Kabir Chakravarti, Soham Acharya, Sumanta Chakraborty, Sudipta Sarkar
hep-th.abstract: The growing catalogue of gravitational wave events enables a statistical analysis of compact binary mergers, typically quantified by the binary merger rate density. This quantity can be influenced by ambient factors, following which, in this work we have investigated the impact of dark matter environment on the merger statistics. We construct a baseline astrophysical model of eccentric and quasi-circular compact binary mergers and extend it by incorporating a model of ultra light dark matter, which affects the orbital evolution of binaries through accretion and dynamical friction. Our analysis of the merged population of binary progenitors demonstrates that, compared to the baseline model, ULDM can potentially alter the merger statistics for ambient non-zero densities, with the best agreement with GWTC-3 obtained for $\rho_0\sim10^6$ GeV/cm$^3$ and eccentricity $\sim0.5$. A comparison with the gravitational wave data from the GWTC-3 catalogue provides crucial insight into potential observational signatures of the ULDM in merger events, leading to possible constraints on the existence and density of dark matter distribution in galaxies.

hep-th.title: On the consistency of non-commutative geometry inspired Reissner-Nordström black hole solution
hep-th.author: Gokhan Alkac, Murat Mesta, Gonul Unal
hep-th.abstract: We revisit the non-commutative geometry inspired Reissner-Nordström black hole solution obtained by smearing the point sources with a Gaussian distribution. We show that while the form of the metric function and the physical properties derived from that remain valid, not all the components of Einstein equations are satisfied: the angular components fail by exactly the Lorentz force density exerted by the electric field on the smeared charge, which the standard electromagnetic energy-momentum tensor leaves unbalanced. We construct an improved energy-momentum tensor that consistently satisfies Einstein equations. It is the unique conserved completion: the standard Maxwell tensor supplemented by an interaction stress supported on the smeared source. The improved tensor leads to a different prediction for the region where the strong energy condition is violated. For certain choice of parameters, our proposal predicts the violation of the energy condition outside the Cauchy horizon, which might be relevant for the stability of the inner horizon and strong cosmic censorship.

hep-th.title: Discrete gravitational diagram technique and corrections to the Newtonian potential
hep-th.author: V.M. Khatsymovsky
hep-th.abstract: To develop a gravitational diagram technique that is ultraviolet finite, we start from Regge's simplicial gravity and use a bell-shaped form of the measure obtained via functional integration over connection. A "hypercubic" structure is considered (some variables are frozen), it is described by the metric $g_{\lambda \mu}$ at the sites. The measure is known in closed form if the timelike length scale is fixed at a low level. This is possible in the synchronous gauge (properly softened to remove nonphysical infrared singularities). This gauge also allows, with a refined finite-difference form of the action, to match the analytical properties of the propagator to the continuum case.The metric is parameterized to make the measure Lebesgue. The linear part of this parametrization leads to a discrete form of standard Feynman diagrams that approximates finite continuum diagrams and is finite for infinite ones; the nonlinear part gives new vertices and diagrams.The maximum of the measure is at the edge length scale $b = b_{\rm s} \sim \eta^{1/2}$, where $\eta$ defines the free factor like $(- \det \|g_{\lambda \mu}\|)^{\eta/2}$ in the measure and should be a large parameter to ensure true action upon integration over connection. For general perturbative expansion (including both that for the measure and the S matrix) to be free of increasing powers of $\eta$, its initial point must be at $b$ sufficiently close to $b_{\rm s}$; this appears to be a dynamic mechanism for establishing $b$ as an optimal initial point of the perturbative expansion.This technique is applied to Newton's potential. Some of new diagrams, including potentially large ones, are mutually cancelled. The S matrix expansion is analyzed to consist of standard diagrams. These diagrams form series with a small parameter $\eta^{-1}$; one-loop diagrams calculated in the literature represent the leading order.

hep-th.title: Resummed energy loss in extreme-mass-ratio scattering using critical orbits
hep-th.author: Leor Barack, Riccardo Gonzo, Benjamin Leather, Oliver Long, Niels Warburton
hep-th.abstract: Motivated by recent efforts to bridge between weak-field and strong-field descriptions of black-hole binary dynamics, we develop a resummation scheme for post-Minkowskian radiative observables in extreme-mass-ratio scattering, augmented with post-Newtonian terms. Specifically, we derive universal interpolation formulas for the total energy emitted in gravitational waves out to infinity and down the event horizon of the large black hole, valid to leading order in the small mass ratio. We test our formulas using numerical results from direct calculations in black hole perturbation theory. The central idea of our approach is to utilize as a strong-field diagnostic the known form of divergence in the radiated energy along geodesics near the parameter-space separatrix between scattering and plunge. The dominant, logarithmic term of this divergence can be expressed in terms of instantaneous energy fluxes calculated along the unstable circular geodesics that form the separatrix, fluxes that we obtain using interpolation of highly accurate numerical data. The same idea could be applied to bound-orbit radiative observables via either unbound-to-bound mapping or a direct resummation of bound-orbit post-Newtonian expressions.

hep-th.title: A new product formula for $(z;q)_\infty$, with applications to asymptotics
hep-th.author: Arash Arabi Ardehali, Hjalmar Rosengren
hep-th.abstract: We express the $q$-Pochhammer symbol $(z;q)_\infty$ as an infinite product of gamma functions, analogously to how Narukawa expressed the elliptic gamma function as an infinite product of hyperbolic gamma functions. This identity is used to obtain asymptotic expansions when $q$ tends to $1$.

hep-th.title: Hall Viscosity in the Quark-Gluon Plasma
hep-th.author: Sukrut Mondkar, Giorgio Torrieri, Matthias Kaminski, René Meyer
hep-th.abstract: We study the Hall viscosity of the quark gluon plasma (QGP) created in non-central heavy-ion collisions. In the presence of a strong magnetic field or vorticity, rotational symmetry is broken from $O(3)$ to $O(2)$, allowing for two independent Hall viscosities associated with shear deformations transverse and parallel to the symmetry-breaking direction. We find the corresponding constitutive relations by extending the kinetic-theory mechanism to three spatial dimensions and provide parametric estimates of the Hall viscosities under realistic QGP conditions. Both kinetic-theory and holographic estimates indicate that Hall viscosities are comparable in magnitude to the shear viscosity at zero magnetic field. We further show that Hall viscous stresses at hydrodynamic initialization can be as large as standard viscous corrections and identify observable consequences in flow and event-plane correlations.

hep-th.title: Axion Quality in Warped Extra-Dimension
hep-th.author: Kiwoon Choi, Chang Hyeon Lee, Chang Sub Shin
hep-th.abstract: We investigate the axion quality problem in warped extra-dimensional models in which the QCD axion arises as the Wilson-line mode of a five-dimensional $U(1)$ gauge field compactified on an $S^1/\mathbb{Z}_2$ orbifold. Higher-dimensional gauge invariance severely constrains possible sources of Peccei--Quinn symmetry breaking, implying that non-QCD contributions to the axion potential are predominantly generated by nonlocal effects mediated by $U(1)$-charged fields propagating along the compact dimension. We systematically compute these contributions and examine how both the warped geometry and the orbifold fixed points (branes) affect the resulting axion quality. Finally, we classify the parametric suppression of the induced axion potential, thereby identifying the conditions under which warped extra-dimensional axions can achieve sufficiently high quality.

hep-th.title: Quantum Charge-4e Superconductivity and Possible Deconfined Pseudocriticality in the Attractive SU(4) Hubbard Model
hep-th.author: Zhou-Quan Wan, Huan Jiang, Xuan Zou, Shiwei Zhang, Shao-Kai Jian
hep-th.abstract: Unlike conventional charge-2e superconductors, a charge-4e superconductor exhibits long-range coherence of electron quartets rather than Cooper pairs. Clear zero-temperature realizations of charge-4e superconductivity remain rare. Here, we investigate the zero-temperature phase diagram of the attractive SU(4) Hubbard model with numerically exact, large-scale quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) simulations overcoming major technical hurdles. We identify both charge-2e and charge-4e superconducting phases. Upon increasing interaction, charge-2e long-range order vanishes, while charge-4e correlations remain robust and converge with system size, establishing a quartet-condensed phase. Interestingly, across the charge-2e--charge-4e transition, single electrons remain gapped, while charge-2e correlations exhibit an effective anomalous dimension substantially exceeding the conventional O(6) Landau theory prediction. These features motivate a fractionalized framework in which the physical charge-2e order parameter is a composite field coupled to an emergent non-Abelian gauge structure. We formulate an Sp(4) gauge-Higgs theory associating the charge-2e and charge-4e states with Higgs and confined phases, respectively. A one-loop analysis of an SU($N_f$) generalization exhibits a fixed-point collision, motivating deconfined pseudocriticality as a possible interpretation of the observed scaling. Our results establish charge-4e superconductivity as a bona fide zero-temperature phase, provide a simple model for future studies in a numerically exact framework, and suggest an unconventional route to superconducting criticality.

hep-th.title: Inaccessibility of the Schwarzschild Singularity to Quantum Probes
hep-th.author: Vishnulal Cheriyodathillathu, Tanmay Patil, Saurya Das, Soumen Basak
hep-th.abstract: We revisit the Schwarzschild singularity in a semiclassical setting where the background geometry is classical and quantum effects enter through Bohmian (quantal) trajectories associated with a Klein-Gordon wave function. Using the Madelung-Bohm decomposition of the Klein-Gordon wavefunction, we show that the quantum-modified motion is equivalent to geodesic motion in an effective metric conformally related to Schwarzschild, with a conformal factor fixed by the wavefunction amplitude. Solving the wavefunction equation near $r\to 0$ determines this factor and yields finite curvature invariants, in suitable coordinates the interior extends smoothly and the effective spacetime is geodesically complete. Our result suggests that quantum probes on a prescribed classical background can experience an operationally regular effective geometry, even though the underlying Schwarzschild spacetime itself remains classically singular.

hep-th.title: Exploring the near-kernel sector of quantum reduced loop gravity
hep-th.author: Ilkka Mäkinen, Hanno Sahlmann, Waleed Sherif
hep-th.abstract: We study the near-kernel sector of the Hamiltonian constraint operator in the one-vertex model of quantum reduced loop gravity using exact diagonalisation methods and variational Monte Carlo methods with neural quantum states. The analysis is based on the symmetric Hamiltonian containing both Euclidean and Lorentzian contributions, and on the variational minimization of the positive quadratic operator $\hat{Q}=\hat{C}^2$, where $\hat{C}$ is the symmetric Hamilton constraint, in truncated Hilbert spaces with spin cutoff up to $j_\text{max}=1001$. In the cases where exact diagonalization is possible, the eigenspace of lowest eigenvalue is one- or two-dimensional, and the eigenvalue, as well as the structure of the eigenstates depends on the cutoff. These ground states are entangled across the three edges. The variational method does not find the lowest eigenspace, but near kernel states, i.e., states with components in a number of low lying eigenspaces. For low cutoffs, they also do not factorize across the three edge degrees of freedom. At larger cutoffs, it increasingly finds near kernel states that factorize over the edges, matched with near-unit fidelity by reduced Thiemann coherent states. We discuss some indication that these states are the optimal near-kernel states if factorization is assumed.

hep-th.title: Collective excitations in quantum gravity condensates
hep-th.author: Andrea Calcinari, Adrià Delhom, Daniele Oriti
hep-th.abstract: A central open problem in quantum gravity is to understand how continuum spacetime emerges from quantum-geometric degrees of freedom in a background-independent setting. A many-body perspective suggests that spacetime emerges as a hydrodynamic phase of many atoms of quantum geometry. This idea underlies several approaches to quantum gravity, and it has been explicitly realised in the group field theory formalism. However, quantum fluctuations beyond the mean-field regime remain largely unexplored. We fill this gap by importing Bogolyubov theory to quantum gravity condensates, showing that leading beyond-mean-field effects manifest as collective excitations, in direct analogy with phonons in laboratory Bose-Einstein condensates. We implement the construction in a tractable group field theory model, where condensates of quantum-geometric atoms reproduce nonsingular expanding cosmologies, and derive the leading beyond-mean-field corrections to the emergent Friedmann dynamics. These results identify a new class of quantum-gravity excitations and establish a controlled bridge between microscopic quantum-gravitational dynamics, many-body collective phenomena, and signatures of spacetime emergence.

hep-th.title: Electromagnetic duality degeneracy in dynamical black hole mergers
hep-th.author: José Ferreira, Gabriele Bozzola, Carlos A. R. Herdeiro, Vasileios Paschalidis, Miguel Zilhão
hep-th.abstract: Electromagnetic duality is a symmetry of the source-free Einstein-Maxwell equations that rotates electric and magnetic fields while leaving the stress-energy tensor invariant. We present the first fully nonlinear realization of this symmetry in dynamical strong-gravity regimes by performing numerical relativity simulations of charged black hole mergers across a continuous duality family. Starting from electrically charged binaries, we generate dyonic and magnetically charged configurations via duality rotations and evolve them within a common numerical framework. We find that all dual configurations exhibit identical spacetime dynamics, while the emitted electromagnetic radiation is related by a rotation of its polarization equal to the duality angle. Our results demonstrate a degeneracy of gravitational observables under electromagnetic duality and provide a concrete mapping between dual configurations at the level of radiation, establishing electromagnetic duality as an organizing principle for dynamical Einstein-Maxwell solutions.

hep-th.title: Revisiting the Axial Anomaly and Chiral Magnetic Effect in Dense Matter, with Applications to Axion Dark Matter
hep-th.author: Deog Ki Hong
hep-th.abstract: We explicitly compute the axial anomaly in dense matter and show that it takes the same form as in vacuum, even in the massless limit. This result follows from a subtle cancellation in the anomalous Ward identity between the medium-induced contributions to the divergence of the axial current and to the pseudoscalar density. We then revisit the chiral magnetic effect in a fermionic medium coupled to an axial chemical potential in an external magnetic field. We show that, in the clean limit, the medium supports a persistent, conserved anomalous current carried by fermions. The current is determined by the axial chemical potential and suppressed by the Fermi velocity, in agreement with anomalous axial-current correlation functions. Finally, we discuss applications to axion physics, where axion dark matter acts as an effective axial chemical potential, and estimate how helicity relaxation by impurity scattering limits the induced current in realistic conductors.

hep-th.title: Energy Extraction via Magnetic Reconnection from a Rotating Dyonic Black Hole in $N = 2, \ U(1)^2$ Gauged Supergravity
hep-th.author: Raid M Suleiman, Shanshan Rodriguez, Dominic O. Chang, Leo Rodriguez
hep-th.abstract: We study energy extraction via magnetic reconnection from a rotating dyonic black hole in four-dimensional $N=2$, $U(1)^2$ gauged supergravity. Using the Comisso-Asenjo mechanism in the ZAMO frame, we derive the asymptotic hydrodynamic energy per unit enthalpy $\epsilon^{\infty}_\pm$ and determine when reconnection outflows attained negative energy at infinity. By varying the spin $a$, electric and magnetic charges, NUT parameter $N_g$, and gauge coupling $g$, we compute the cutoff magnetization $\sigma_0^{\rm cutoff}$ and map the region of parameter space that admits $\epsilon^{\infty}_-<0$. We find that $\sigma_0^{\rm cutoff}$ and the very existence of Comisso-Asenjo extraction are tightly controlled by $g$ and the dyonic charges: increasing $g$ or pushing the charges toward extremality raises $\sigma_0^{\rm cutoff}$ and shrinks the CA-active part of the ergoregion. Unlike Kerr, the spin enters through the normalization factor $\Xi$, and the quartic horizon function $\Delta_g$, so geometric effects from the AdS/NUT deformation dominate the usual frame-dragging enhancement. As a result, the extracted power and efficiency are non-monotonic in $a$ and peak at intermediate spin ($a\sim0.8$); near-extremal rotation is not required for high efficiency, provided $g$ is small and $Q$ is moderate. Efficient extraction further demands extreme magnetization and nearly radial outflows, confining the active reconnection layer to a thin shell, just outside the horizon.

hep-th.title: Fermion mass relations in one-parameter modular models
hep-th.author: Salvador Centelles Chuliá, Xueqi Li, Xiang-Gan Liu, Omar Medina, J. T. Penedo
hep-th.abstract: Modular flavour symmetries provide a possible organizing principle for the Standard Model Yukawa sector, by replacing generic couplings with a potentially small number of modular forms controlled by a single complex modulus. We study the extreme limit of this idea: One-Parameter Models, in which each charged-fermion mass matrix is fixed by a single modular invariant contraction. We develop a systematic method to construct such models, showing that the One-Parameter Model requirement is already highly constraining at the level of possible fermion hierarchies. In a concrete realization, the charged-lepton and down-quark sectors are controlled by the common modulus, leading to exact mass relations at the flavour scale, $m_s^5 = 2\sqrt{2}\,m_d^3m_b^2, \qquad m_\mu^3 = \sqrt{2}\,m_e m_\tau^2, \qquad m_s^2m_\tau = \sqrt{2}\,m_e m_b^2$. We show that, once renormalization-group evolution and selective supersymmetric threshold effects are included, these high-scale relations can be made compatible with low-energy charged-fermion data. Our results provide a working proof of principle for One-Parameter Models and point towards a possible route to the flavour puzzle through highly constrained constructions.

hep-th.title: Exclusive Quark and Gluon Dijet Production as Probes of GPDs at Collider Energies
hep-th.author: Zhuoyi Pang, Paweł Sznajder, Lech Szymanowski, Jakub Wagner
hep-th.abstract: We study exclusive electroproduction of dijets in the collinear factorization framework as a probe of generalized parton distributions (GPDs). For quark dijet production, we extend previous analyses by including contributions from helicity GPDs and by assessing an additional leading-order electromagnetic channel governed by elastic nucleon form factors. Furthermore, we investigate exclusive gluon dijet production. We compare our prediction to HERA data and provide projections for measurements at the future Electron-Ion Collider.

hep-th.title: ACT-DR6 consistent inflation in generalised entropic cosmology and $f(Q)$ gravity
hep-th.author: Shin'ichi Nojiri, Sergei D. Odintsov
hep-th.abstract: Within the framework of generalised entropic cosmology and its equivalent $f(Q)$ gravity, we construct inflationary scenarios consistent with recent Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT) observations combined with Planck-BAO data. We work with $f(Q)$ gravity and use the reconstruction scheme from which one can obtain an arbitrary cosmological evolution consistent with desirable theoretical or observational considerations. Explicit inflationary cosmologies of the above theory, which pass ACT-Data Release 6 (DR6) data combined with Planck and BAO, are obtained. For $f(Q)$ gravity coupled with scalar, we obtain ACT inflation for large classes of $f(Q)$ via the choice of the scalar potentials. The entropic cosmology based on generalised entropy, which includes most of the known entropies like Tsallis, Rényi, Barrow, etc as a particular case, is investigated. The corresponding FRW equations, depending on the parameters of generalised entropy, are presented. Using the correspondence between the generalised entropy and $f(Q)$ gravity, we obtain generalised entropic inflation, which is consistent with the ACT-DR6. At the next step, the entropic gravity coupled with scalar is considered. It is demonstrated how one can obtain ACT-DR6-consistent inflation for such a theory based on any generalised entropy considered in this paper via the choice of scalar potentials. These findings may point towards the correct unifying entropy of the early universe.

hep-th.title: Phonon Angular Momentum Pumping in Curved Membranes
hep-th.author: Pablo A. Morales
hep-th.abstract: Flexural vibrations dominate the low-energy spectrum of a flat crystalline membrane but do not couple to phonon Hall viscosity. We show that static curvature couples normal motion to in-plane strain, allowing an oscillatory flexural drive to generate elliptical in-plane motion and pump phonon angular momentum along the surface normal. A net angular momentum persists in randomly rippled membranes, with its magnitude and handedness controlled by the drive and ripple spectra. Transfer of the pumped angular momentum to the support produces a steady torque that reverses with the magnetic field and scales with the mean-square curvature. Using the measured bulk Hall viscosity of $\alpha$-RuCl$_3$ to set the scale, we estimate a torque of order $10^{-23}$--$10^{-22}\,\mathrm{N\,m}$ for a few-layer membrane, within reach of demonstrated torsional sensors. The same flexural-to-shear response provides a probe of phonon Hall viscosity in atomically thin crystals.

hep-th.title: Landau Levels on the Surface of a Cube
hep-th.author: Almila Kura, Bayram Tekin, Mehmet Özgür Oktel
hep-th.abstract: We study the quantum mechanics of a charged particle confined to the surface of a cube enclosing a magnetic monopole. The magnetic field is chosen to have a constant magnitude on each face and to point along the outward normal, preserving the rotational symmetry of the cube. We formulate the continuum problem using two gauge patches on the cube surface and show that consistency of the wavefunction gives the Dirac quantization condition. Since an explicit vector potential does not remain invariant under ordinary rotations, we construct gauge-modified rotation operators and use them to classify the eigenstates. Even monopole charges are described by the irreducible representations of the cubic rotation group O, while odd monopole charges require the spinorial representations of the binary octahedral group 2O. We compute the spectrum with a gauge-covariant finite-difference discretization and find Landau-level-like manifolds whose degeneracies are split by the discrete cubic symmetry. We also study the corresponding tight-binding Hofstadter problem on the discretized cube. The resulting spectrum contains the usual magnetic subband structure together with additional gap states localized near the cube corners.

hep-th.title: How does geometry shape quantum emission in rotating bumblebee gravity?
hep-th.author: A. A. Araújo Filho
hep-th.abstract: We compare propagation and static emission estimates in a rotating metric geometry and a stationary metric-affine bumblebee geometry. Their distinct constructions and spatial asymptotics are kept, and normalized Killing times define the physical frequencies and angular velocities. Direct invariant calculations identify the metric-affine outer root and open exterior axes as curvature singularities for generic rotation. The obstruction at bifurcation surface poles concerns the smoothness of the bumblebee field independently. Its mixed meridional component couples angular channels; finite transverse energy fixes the adopted axial condition and defines a self adjoint stationary operator on bounded exterior annuli. For the metric geometry, we construct normalized radiative scalar modes with specified Unruh data, evaluate the horizon frequency transformation, and include spontaneous superradiant emission through the radial scattering map. We prove positivity of the axisymmetric potential and compute numerical transmission factors and a partial scalar energy spectrum alongside an analytical lower bound. The static emission estimates use the stated Stefan-Boltzmann model.

hep-th.title: A No-Go Theorem for Order-Two Clifford Electric-Magnetic Duality
hep-th.author: Shunta Takahashi, Zhi Li, Beni Yoshida
hep-th.abstract: Electromagnetic duality in the toric code has order two at the level of anyon types and acts as a Hadamard-type logical transformation on the encoded quantum information. Here, we ask whether it can likewise be realized microscopically as an order-two Clifford operation. For the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ toric code, we prove that any locality-preserving Clifford realization of electric-magnetic exchange cannot have order two. Our proof is fully general and requires neither translation symmetry with restricted families of system sizes nor a fixed pairing between vertex and plaquette stabilizers. Geometrically, the proof locally emulates the unavoidable crossing between electric and magnetic strings, similar to a cross-cap in a non-orientable manifold. Extending the problem to the $\mathbb{Z}_N$ toric code, we find that an order-two Clifford realization exists for odd $N$, whereas it is impossible for even $N$. Our result shows that the order-two exchange of closed-string operators cannot be extended to an order-two exchange of open-string operators.

hep-th.title: No Einstein Relation, No Problem: How Relativistic Weakly Coupled Heavy Quarks Equilibrate Beyond Leading Logarithm Anyway
hep-th.author: Jean F. Du Plessis, Bruno Scheihing-Hitschfeld
hep-th.abstract: Relativistic heavy quarks equilibrate even when their microscopic drag and momentum diffusion violate the Einstein relation. We investigate how equilibration proceeds as a function of the coupling and compared to simplified Fokker-Planck models. To do this, we present a detailed calculation of the momentum-transfer kernel in weakly coupled non-Abelian plasmas through strict $\mathcal{O}(g^4)$, and study the resulting dynamics at leading order in the inverse heavy-quark mass. Beyond leading logarithm, its non-Gaussian structure plays a crucial role in equilibration. We examine closely the analytic structure of the evolution kernel, determine the large-order asymptotics of the momentum-transfer cumulants, and show how the kernel's bounded analytic domain fixes asymmetric exponential tails at the level of the momentum transfer probability. Strongly coupled $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM also features an approximately Gaussian core and exponential tails, but differs in the nature of the kernel's singularities and the velocity dependence of the transport coefficients and tail exponents. These differences have distinct dynamical consequences: for the parameters studied, the persistence of the relativistic population in steeply falling spectra is largely explained by drag alone at very weak coupling, whereas fluctuation-induced survivor bias produces a large relative enhancement at strong coupling. Nevertheless, the shared qualitative structure between weak and strong coupling points the way towards a practical phenomenological description of heavy quarks anchored in first-principles field theory.

hep-th.title: Self-Interacting Dark Matter: From Particle Physics Theories to Structure Formation Simulations
hep-th.author: Martin Rosenlyst, Vinh Tran, Oliver Zier, Xuejian Shen, Mark Vogelsberger, Thejs Brinckmann, Mads T. Frandsen, Jesús Zavala, Frederik Holt Dihver Christensen, Mikkel Theiss Kristensen
hep-th.abstract: We establish a unified theory-to-simulation framework for self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) that integrates three components: (i) a comprehensive, self-contained treatment of its particle-physics foundations and a broad range of model classes; (ii) a systematic, quantitative mapping from microscopic dark-sector physics to structure-formation simulation inputs through explicit expressions and numerical prescriptions; and (iii) the development, implementation, and validation of a broad suite of SIDM algorithms and a dedicated DM decay module in the moving-mesh code AREPO-2. Under (i), we detail the particle content, symmetries, interactions, production mechanisms, and constraints of a broad landscape of elementary and composite SIDM models, and present representative viable benchmark models. Under (ii), the mapping specifies cosmological initial conditions, internal-state masses and populations, reaction networks, velocity- and angle-dependent cross sections, dissipative energy loss, and decay rates and recoil kinematics. We then apply this mapping to a broad range of SIDM model classes. Under (iii), we implement and validate SIDM algorithms with constant and velocity-dependent cross sections, covering isotropic and anisotropic scattering, multi-state elastic and inelastic reactions, and dissipative processes, alongside a dedicated DM decay module in AREPO-2. We validate the implementations through beam-lattice deflection, thermalization and decay tests, isolated-halo gravothermal core-collapse simulations, and cosmological box and zoom-in simulations. The results recover analytical predictions and published benchmarks and demonstrate agreement across numerical schemes. Our theory-to-simulation framework serves as a cross-disciplinary reference and a practical bridge between SIDM particle physics and simulations of nonlinear structure formation.

hep-th.title: Rapid Graviton Thermalization through a Scalar--Gauss--Bonnet Coupling
hep-th.author: Hongguang Zhang, Zhengyang Qiu, Sirui Wang, Jiayi Wei
hep-th.abstract: We show that gravitons can thermalize much faster than the universe expands in an effective scalar-mediated model. A thermal fermion bath maintains a massive scalar close to equilibrium, while scalar decay and inverse decay, $\phi\rightleftarrows g+g$, drive the graviton distribution toward a Bose--Einstein distribution with zero chemical potential. We establish this equilibrium state and calculate how it is reached from an initially empty graviton sector. For a scalar mass of $1\,{\rm TeV}$, an interaction scale $\Lambda_{\rm int}=m_\phi/0.03$, and a Yukawa coupling $y=0.03$, the graviton occupations approach their equilibrium values to within $0.1\%$ over $0.1\leq p/T\leq5$ after approximately $0.024$ initial Hubble times, including cosmic expansion and energy transfer from the bath. This interval contains the thermal energy-spectrum peak. The scalar remains close to equilibrium, its vacuum decay widths are narrow, and the graviton interaction is perturbative over the reaction domain. Assuming the effective theory applies on this domain, our results demonstrate that gravitons can reach near-thermal equilibrium under these conditions. We also derive the present-day thermal spectrum for a specified decoupling and entropy history.

hep-th.title: MadStree: automated evaluation of tree-level de Sitter correlators
hep-th.author: Jiaqi Chen, Yi-Xiao Tao, Xinyi Wang, Dong Zhang
hep-th.abstract: We first derived the formulae of recursive reduction and d log-form differential equations for arbitrary tree-level and loop-integrand cosmological correlators, taking the external relations of massless bulk propagators into consideration. The differential equations could be systematically solved and provide the efficient evaluation of them. We have implemented this methodology as a Mathematica package MadStree. To demonstrate the efficiency of our method, we evaluated up to $10^6$ points for each master integral in our examples, and found that the average computational cost per numerical point per master integral is on the order of $\mu\mathrm{s}$.

hep-th.title: Massive Scalar Quasinormal Modes and Quasibound States of Charged Black Holes with Logarithmic corrections
hep-th.author: Prosenjit Paul, Rickmoy Samanta
hep-th.abstract: We study how long-range deformations in a black-hole metric affect the oscillation, trapping, and decay of a neutral, minimally coupled massive scalar field. We choose a logarithmic deformation of Reissner-Nordström (RN) sourced by nonlinear electrodynamics, arising as an exact solution of Einstein gravity. The same geometry also arises in a phenomenological perfect-fluid dark-matter model. We provide several exact completions of this geometry with finite Arnowitt-Deser-Misner (ADM) mass. Focusing on the original logarithmic geometry, we analyze both quasinormal modes (QNMs), which describe relaxation, and quasibound states (QBSs), which describe trapped modes with small horizon absorption. We first show that a small scalar mass moves the potential barrier outward, raises it, and reduces its curvature. First-order WKB then predicts weaker damping at every fixed finite multipole and overtone. We then compare several approaches, namely sixth-order WKB, global matching, a generalized Leaver method (adapted to the logarithmic geometry) and time-domain evolution. All methods yield consistent QNM estimates within their ranges of validity. Global matching and Leaver also agree closely for QBSs. Further analytic estimates with a reference trapped state show that a local Padé approximation gives a binding-energy error of about $0.04\%$, while leading Gamow tunnelling underestimates damping by about $25\%$. Across the sampled QBSs, increasing the scalar mass or nonlinear coupling strengthens binding but shortens the lifetime through greater horizon absorption. Finally, using an appropriate horizon regularization and a common complex radial contour, we demonstrate orthogonality of an independently computed QNM-QBS pair using a suitable relativistic bilinear framework.

hep-th.title: Particle dynamics in rotating charged Bumblebee black holes: An analytical correspondence with Kerr-Newman
hep-th.author: Deyou Chen, Chuang Yang
hep-th.abstract: In this paper, we establish an analytical correspondence between the equatorial dynamics of spinless and spinning test particles in a slowly rotating charged Einstein--Bumblebee black hole spacetime and those in an effective Kerr--Newman spacetime. For spinning particles, the correspondence is established within the Mathisson--Papapetrou--Dixon framework under appropriate parameter matching. We show that corresponding circular orbits have identical radii and coordinate angular velocities, while their radial dynamics and local instability rates exhibit a Lorentz-violation-dependent scaling. Nevertheless, the correspondence does not imply complete dynamical equivalence, as orbital trajectories and radial perturbation growth over an azimuthal period generally differ. These results delineate the scope and limitations of the effective Kerr--Newman correspondence by distinguishing the dynamical properties preserved under parameter matching from those modified by the Lorentz-violating radial deformation.
